At FirstClub, we are building a new kind of quick commerce from the ground up, and the supply chain is where that promise is won or lost. The Supply Chain Product team builds the systems that decide what we buy, where it sits, how it moves and what we promise each member. Every order that reaches a member on time, fresh and complete is the output of our products.


The team's charter spans the full supply chain:


- Buying & Sourcing: demand-led purchase planning, vendor management, PO lifecycle and inbound scheduling.


- Collection Centers: first-mile intake, quality checks, grading and consolidation of fresh and farm produce.


- Distribution Centers (DCs): inbound, putaway, storage, picking, packing, outbound and returns.


- Middle Mile: DC-to-Club House replenishment, trip planning, vehicle utilization and inventory movement.


- Club Houses: receiving, storage, pick-pack, cycle counts, freshness and wastage control.


- Inventory Management: single source of truth for stock, ageing and expiry, replenishment and inventory accuracy across nodes.


- Capacity Management: labor, slot, storage and throughput planning across nodes and time of day.


- Promise Engine: what we promise each member availability and delivery ETA based on live inventory and capacity.


Why FirstClub


- Build, don't babysit: Much of our supply chain stack is being built right now. You will design core systems, not just tune someone else's.


- Small team, big surface area: You'll own outcomes that would sit with a whole team at a larger company.


- Fast loops: Ship on Monday, watch it run on a Club House floor by Wednesday, improve it by Friday.


- Ground truth over slide decks: Our PMs spend real time in DCs, Collection Centers and Club Houses, not just in dashboards.


- Scrappy beats perfect: We'd rather run a pilot this week than polish a plan for next quarter.


- Your fingerprints on the company: The decisions you make now shape how FirstClub scales to every new city.


The role


As a Senior Product Manager, you will own the end-to-end supply chain product charter at FirstClub from how we source and buy, through Collection Centers, DCs and the middle mile, to inventory in our Club Houses and the promise we make each member. Your mandate is to build a high-control, intelligent and scalable supply chain that improves availability, freshness and speed while driving down cost per order and wastage.


This isn't a role where you inherit a mature platform and keep it running. You'll build core pieces of FirstClub's supply chain while the business grows around them: making calls with incomplete data, getting your hands dirty on the floor, and setting how product works across the charter. You'll shape how inventory moves across the network, how frontline teams work, and how FirstClub scales to new cities without losing control or quality.


What you will do


- Own the product vision, strategy and roadmap across Buying & Sourcing, Collection Centers, DCs, Middle Mile, Club Houses, Inventory Management, Capacity Management and the Promise Engine.


- Set and own the north-star metrics for the charter: availability and fill rate, promise adherence (promised vs. actual), inventory accuracy, days of inventory, wastage and shrinkage, cost per order and throughput per node.


- Partner deeply with Supply Chain, Category, Operations and Finance leadership to find the biggest ground-level problems and convert them into a prioritised, outcome-driven roadmap.


- Architect the core systems with Engineering: a single source of truth for inventory across nodes, a demand-led buying and replenishment engine, and a Promise Engine that balances availability, capacity and speed in real time.


- Build capacity planning across labour, slots, storage and vehicles, so the network flexes for peaks, new categories and new cities.


- Own the frontline tooling strategy for associates, site managers, QC teams and transport partners making work simpler, faster and measurable, including productivity tracking and incentives.


- Lead build-vs-buy decisions across WMS, TMS, procurement and planning systems, and drive integrations with vendors and 3P partners.


- Treat AI and automation as first principles, not add-ons: forecasting, auto-replenishment, intelligent allocation, anomaly and shrinkage detection, and agentic workflows that remove manual decisions from planners and site teams.


- Run a strong experimentation and measurement culture pilots by node or city, clear success criteria, and rigorous readouts.


- Lead, coach and grow a team of Product Managers, raising the bar on problem framing, execution, stakeholder management and ground-level empathy.


- Help shape the operating model for scaling FirstClub's supply chain across cities with high reliability and healthy unit economics.


What we are looking for


- 5 to 8 years of Product Management experience, with a track record of owning and scaling products with measurable business impact.


- Experience leading or mentoring Product Managers, and happy to be a player-coach who still owns hands-on product work.


- Deep experience in supply chain, warehousing, quick commerce, e-commerce, grocery, food delivery or logistics, ideally across more than one node of the chain.


- Strong understanding of inventory planning, replenishment, warehouse operations, middle-mile logistics, capacity planning or delivery promise systems.


- Experience building products with a significant frontline or ground operations component.


- Proven ability to move operational and financial metrics such as fill rate, wastage, cost per order, productivity and SLA adherence.


- Strong analytical depth: comfortable with SQL, experimentation and working alongside Data Science on forecasting and optimisation problems.


- An AI-native mindset: you think naturally about how ML, automation and agents can change how decisions get made, not just how screens look.


- Excellent stakeholder management with senior Operations, Category, Finance and Engineering leaders.


- You thrive in early-stage, fast-moving environments: you'll write the spec, pull the data and walk the floor yourself, and you know the answer is usually a mix of technology, process and operational change.


- Bachelor's degree in engineering, Computer Science, Business, Economics or a related field. An MBA is a plus; strong product experience matters more.


Good to have


- Built or scaled a WMS, inventory platform, procurement system, TMS or promise/ETA engine.


- Experience with fresh, perishable and cold-chain supply chains, including FEFO, grading and expiry management.


- Exposure to demand forecasting, replenishment optimization, slotting, network planning or routing.


- Experience launching and scaling operations across multiple cities and high daily order volumes.


- Experience building frontline workforce products: productivity tracking, incentives, gamification or training.


- Experience shipping AI/ML-driven decisioning or agentic workflows in production operations.

About the role:

Key responsibilities:

1. Product definition and roadmap

  • Own and evolve well-scoped features in core VMDR modules such as Asset Discovery & Inventory, Vulnerability Detection (Cloud Agent, network scanners, passive sensors), TruRisk Prioritization (QDS, threat intel, CISA KEV, EPSS), Dashboards & Reporting, and Remediation (Patch Management, TruRisk Eliminate).

Platform support engineering moves into this function, with a small internal team retaining oversight while the vendor operates more than 30 platforms and the data fabric under an OTO model. Seventeen roles.

What makes this role different. The delivery management layer between the Principals and the analysts in a practice judged on throughput and turnaround, not just rigour. You own review scheduling and reviewer allocation against incoming demand, drive findings to closure across every domain, and run the governance reporting and audit evidence packs. Workflow automation in ServiceNow is how the practice scales, and improving it is part of the role. You carry a review caseload alongside the management load, so this is not a pure coordination job.

Key Responsibilities

This role will provide you the opportunity to lead key activities to progress your career. These responsibilities include some of the following:

  • Manage the demand pipeline across two Principals and the domain analysts, and decide what gets expedited - including telling a programme director that their review will not be.
  • Manage assurance throughput, turnaround and SLA metrics the function is judged on, and escalate capacity pressure before turnaround slips quietly.
  • Drive findings and time-bound conditions to closure across all domains, chasing the ones that stall and escalating aged items by name.
  • Develop the analyst teams domain depth and progression, in a practice where most reviewers arrive strong in one domain and need two.
  • Own the quality of what the practice produces - review rigour, finding clarity and closure discipline - and correct it at the individual level when it drops.
  • Carry a review caseload alongside the management load, so technical credibility with the Principals is maintained.
  • Manage the analyst teams day-to-day workload, quality and development across their domain specialisms.
  • Carry roughly a third of a reviewer caseload yourself on Tier 2 designs, so allocation decisions are informed by current technical judgement rather than administration.
  • Verify against standards the practice does not write, and protect that separation in how work is allocated.
  • Spot capacity pressure in the pipeline two sprints out and escalate it, rather than letting turnaround slip quietly and explaining it afterwards.
  • Use approved AI tools in your day-to-day work to improve your own productivity and your teams ways of working, sharing what works and applying sound judgement, including validating outputs and following GSKs Responsible AI, privacy and security requirements.

Basic Qualifications

  • 10+ years in cyber security or technology assurance, including team management - domain focus: Design Assurance practice delivery across all Cyber Architecture and Solutions security domains
  • Managing delivery across Principals and analysts - review scheduling and reviewer allocation against demand, using workflow automation
  • Tracking findings to closure with throughput and turnaround metrics, and running practice governance reporting and audit evidence packs

  • Managing AI and agentic tool reviews within the practice, and setting the evidence standard those reviews must meet.

Overview

Overview

Small businesses drive the global economy. In the US, SMBs employ 60% of the labor force and create 80% of new jobs. However, the stakes are high, as 1 in 2 businesses will fail to survive within their first five years. In an environment where time is money, precise time tracking for payroll, invoicing, and project management is the critical lever for maintaining profitability and growing the business.

Within QuickBooks, our Workforce platform fuels productivity for growing teams — from time tracking and scheduling to project management and field operations. With 30M+ employees in the QuickBooks ecosystem and 18M paid through Workforce Solutions, we are building the essential tools that empower frontline teams and help businesses turn time into money.

Opportunity

We are seeking a Staff Product Manager to lead the verticalization of QuickBooks Time. You’ll make our time tracking platform the system of record for hours, labor cost, and payroll in the industries where labor is the highest cost, starting with construction and field services. Time is the source of hours for the entire QuickBooks ecosystem. Customers use the hours their teams track to run payroll, bill for their work, and understand whether each job is making money, and the mid-market businesses we serve need all three to work together without spreadsheets or re-entry.

This is a high-ownership role. You will own three connected areas end to end: time to payroll, so approved hours, overtime, and pay items flow into QuickBooks Payroll accurately and automagically; job costing, so every hour tracked produces labor cost estimates against projects and budgets before payroll runs and accurate actuals after it; and worker time tracking across Workforce Web, Workforce Kiosk, and the Workforce mobile app, where millions of workers track their time. You will build on Time 2.0, our rebuilt time platform that now lives inside QuickBooks Online, and extend it so that serving a new industry is mostly configuration rather than new code.

We need a scrappy, customer-obsessed product leader who leads through influence. Someone who navigates dependencies across Payroll, Projects, Mid-Market, and Payments, earns the trust and confidence of our customers and accountants, and ships experiences that delight both the worker clocking in on a job site and the admin who approves time and runs payroll.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities

Vertical Strategy. Own the multi-year roadmap for verticalizing QuickBooks Time, starting with construction and field services. Translate how each industry runs its labor (jobs, cost codes, phases, and certified payroll on a construction site; jobs, visits, and dispatch in field services) into shared platform concepts and configurable experiences, so that each new vertical is mostly configuration rather than new code. Decide what we build, what we configure, and where partner integrations fill the gap.
Time to Payroll. Own the flow of hours from clock-in to paycheck. Make approved time, overtime and break policies, and pay items land in QuickBooks Payroll accurately and automatically, with no exports, syncs, or re-entry, and make approvals fast and trustworthy for a mid-market company with hundreds of employees.
Job Costing: Estimates and Actuals. Deliver real-time labor costing that owners, project managers, and accountants trust. Partner with Projects, Payroll, and Accounting so that time is the single source of hours for payroll, invoicing, and profitability reporting.
Worker Time Tracking. Own how workers track time across Workforce Web, Workforce Kiosk, and the Workforce mobile app, where millions of workers already track their hours. Deliver one consistent, reliable experience for clocking in and out, breaks, schedules, geofencing, and job and task selection that holds up on a job site with poor connectivity and for crews whose first language is not English, and complete the migration of workers off legacy TSheets surfaces onto the new platform.
Commercial Impact. Own the metrics for your area: Time adoption within Workforce Premium and Elite offerings, attached in mid-market and industry editions. Plus worker engagement across web, kiosk, and mobile. Use data and customer evidence to prioritize, measure what ships, and make Time and real-time job costing a central part of how QuickBooks is sold to construction and field services customers, a market where competitors generate $150M+ ARR.
Operational Velocity. Run the end-to-end product lifecycle for your area: write crisp requirements, pressure-test designs, manage edge cases, and drive alignment across engineering, design, data, go-to-market, and customer success teams in the US and India. You lead through influence rather than authority, and you are fluent in AI-native tools like Claude and Cursor, using them to move faster from insight to shipped product.
Customer Empathy. Be the voice of the business owner, the payroll admin, and the frontline worker. Spend time with customers on their job sites and with the accountants who recommend HCM products to their clients, and make sure every feature removes a real pain point in how they bid, schedule, track, pay, and get paid.

Qualifications

Qualifications

A Product Leader. 8+ years of product management craft, including ownership of a complex, multi-team product area as a senior individual contributor. You have a proven track record of building and scaling customer-facing products in HCM, workforce management, construction or field service software, or fintech.
Strategic & Influential. You possess strong executive presence, translating market and customer insight into a strategy and roadmap that align senior stakeholders and technical teams. You make bold bets and bring partner teams along without direct authority.
Domain Depth. You understand how labor-intensive businesses run: how hours become payroll, how time, cost rates, and pay types become job costs, and how estimates compare to actuals. Experience with payroll, time and attendance, job costing, or construction and field service workflows is a strong advantage.
A Proven Growth Driver. You have a track record of spearheading complex initiatives that deliver measurable business growth. You understand the levers of adoption, attach, ARPC, and retention, and you use them to prioritize and to drive P&L growth.
An Ambitious Problem Solver. You proactively anticipate customer and stakeholder needs, thrive in ambiguity and turn complex, messy friction into clear roadmaps. You are scrappy and effective at managing a portfolio of bets across the lifecycle, from 0-1 innovations to products at scale. You know when to push forward and when to pivot based on evidence and stakeholder feedback.
Customer Obsessed & Analytical. You possess deep empathy for small and mid-market business operations and frontline workforce challenges. You combine this heart with rigorous analytical aptitude, storytelling with data to prioritize investments.
Technical Fluency. You demonstrate strong product judgment and comfort engaging across technical topics to build reliable web, mobile, and kiosk products on a shared platform, including APIs, data models, and integrations with payroll and accounting systems. Experience with agentic AI, payment systems, or HCM platforms is an advantage.
Education. BA or BS degree is required, and an MBA or advanced degree is preferred.

2Base Technologies Pvt. Ltd. is a Kochi-based IT services and software development company established in 2010. We are a full-service technology partner offering technology consulting, custom software development, enterprise application development, web and mobile application development, and digital transformation solutions. We have delivered across Insurance, EdTech, Hospitality, and Travel & Tourism, and we work with clients in global markets including the US and UK.

The Opportunity

We are building our own technology products, with a strong focus on AI-driven solutions, and we are looking for the person who will own what they become. This is a product at the concept and early development stage. You will shape its direction, validate the market opportunity, decide what is built and what is not, and drive it towards commercial success.
As our first dedicated Product Management professional, you will also establish the product function at 2Base: there is no existing roadmap, process or product organisation to inherit.

Key Responsibilities

Define the product vision, strategy, roadmap and long-term direction, and keep the roadmap stable enough to plan against and open enough to change when the evidence changes.
Conduct market research, competitor analysis, and customer discovery to identify and validate product opportunities, and bring the findings into roadmap decisions rather than filing them as reports.
Translate customer problems and business needs into clear product requirements: the outcome and the user problem, specified well enough for Engineering to build against without dictating the solution.
Own feature prioritisation and release decisions with Engineering and UI/UX, and be able to state the cost and the benefit of each choice. A roadmap that only says yes is a backlog.
Identify and evaluate AI, Generative AI and automation opportunities, and assess each on feasibility, scalability, cost and business value before it reaches the roadmap.
Define product success metrics before the work starts, instrument the product to measure them, and read the results honestly afterwards.
Contribute to product positioning, pricing, go-to-market strategy and commercial viability, working with Sales and Marketing.
Build shared context across the organisation so that teams can make decisions without routing every question through you.
Work closely with the Founder, Engineering, UI/UX, Sales and other stakeholders to align on product direction and drive execution.

What You Will Not Own
​
Product Manager and Project Manager are used interchangeably across the market. At 2Base, they are different roles, so the boundary is stated rather than assumed.
Client project delivery. Project Managers own client engagements, schedules, and escalations.
Engineering architecture and implementation. You own what and why; Engineering owns how. Where the two conflict, you negotiate rather than instruct.
UI/UX design execution. The design function designs. You own the user outcome and brief, review and decide against it.
Final product investment and budget approval. The Founder decides what the product is funded to do and over what horizon. You own the case that decision is taken on.
Client-specific commercial negotiations. Pricing and packaging of the product itself is yours; client contracts are not.

Requirements
Experience

6–12 years in the technology industry, with at least 4 years in Product Management or direct product ownership.
At least one product you took from concept or early development to actual customer usage, with a clear view of what happened after release. A product you inherited fully formed and maintained is a weaker signal than a smaller one you shaped.
A decision not to build something, and what it cost you to hold that line.
Direct work with engineering teams through a build, not across a handover, with enough understanding of software development, technical feasibility, APIs, integrations and cloud applications to judge what a decision will cost.
AI and Emerging Technology
Practical exposure to AI-powered products, Generative AI, machine learning or automation-driven solutions.
The ability to tell a capability apart from a product, and to assess an AI use case on feasibility, scalability, cost and business value rather than on novelty.
Product Judgement

You can describe how you decided what to build: the evidence you had, the evidence you wanted and did not have, and what you did about the gap.
You can reason about a product commercially. Who pays, what for, and what has to be true for the numbers to work.
You can hold a position with a founder, an engineering lead or a client, and change it when the argument against you is the better one. Knowing which situation you are in is the skill.
You write and present clearly. Most of a product manager's influence here travels as writing, and a requirement that is ambiguous on Monday becomes an argument three weeks later.
Ways of Working
You start by asking rather than deciding. The first months are spent understanding users, the business model, what has already been attempted, and how decisions are actually made here.
You work independently and establish your own processes. There is no research function and no analyst to brief.
You influence without formal authority. Nobody in this structure reports to you, and the roadmap holds because people agree with it.
You can make a decision that leaves someone unhappy, explain the reasoning, and keep working with them. Trade-offs are the job, and somebody loses every time one is made.
Education

A Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

What We Are Not Looking For
Stated now rather than at the end of a multi-stage process.
Project or delivery managers looking to change title. The skills overlap less than the market suggests, and this is not a promotion path from delivery.
Business analysts who have written specifications against requirements someone else set. Valuable work; different work.
Candidates whose account of a product is the features it shipped, with no view on whether it should have shipped them.
Anyone who needs an established research function, design system and process in place before they can start.

Benefits
A growth-driven environment with opportunities to lead, innovate, and upskill continuously.

jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
About the company

Openprovider is an ICANN-accredited domain registrar and technology company founded in 2004 in Rotterdam, Netherlands.

We are a fully-remote organization with more than 90 team members spread across 20+ countries.

A diverse and inclusive organization, we support a healthy work/life balance and are constantly looking for new ways to help the well-being of our people. We support a flexible schedule and are 100% performance and result-oriented.

At Openprovider, we're not just a company; we're a mission-driven team dedicated to transforming the domain industry. We believe in providing a trusted digital identity to every business.

Our innovative approach is reshaping the industry from a traditional transactional model to a more customer-centric, subscription-based approach. We pay subscriptions for music, newspapers, and movies - why should domains be any different?

Our vision is to build a place where curious, self-driven people do their best work together, to deliver on our mission: a reliable, free, and secure online world for every customer we serve. Our world is changing fast, especially with AI, and we see that as an opportunity to stay ahead of change, shape it and create more value for our customers.

Our values

Be a wolf, not a sheep: we value the entrepreneurial spirit in everyone.
Knowledge equals power: we are constantly hungry to learn, for ourselves and our customers.
Enjoy what you do and do what you enjoy: we want work to be something you look forward to.
Quality results in quantity: we care about excellence and attention to detail.
TEAM, Together everyone achieves more: collaboration is how we get our best results.
Come join us on our journey to create a trusted digital world.

About the role

In this role, you’ll build a profitable and sustainable products business alongside our domains portfolio. Your scope will include SSL certificates, Email and Plesk as commercial product lines, as well as the RCP (reseller control panel) journeys that enable our resellers to purchase, provision, manage and renew these products.

You’ll be accountable for their financial performance and quality, while managing supplier partnerships to keep our offering competitive and future-proof. The role reports to the Director of Product.

Key responsibilities

Own the SSL, Email and Plesk portfolio and P&L: positioning, assortment, pricing proposals (with Pricing and Finance), margin and lifecycle decisions from launch to sunset.

Own supplier partnerships with Certificate Authorities, our email platform provider and Plesk/WebPros: contracts, volume tiers, rebates, SLAs, roadmap alignment and escalations.

Grow adoption across our reseller base through cross-sell with domains and hosting, bundles, purchase journey placement and launches with Sales and Marketing.

Run product initiatives as structured projects, including supplier integrations, API changes and compliance changes such as CA/B Forum rules.

Shape the product roadmap with a commercial lens and partner with Engineering on delivery.

Track results against clear targets: margin and revenue per product line, attach and renewal rates, and on-time delivery of milestones and roadmap items.

What we are looking for

Competences

Hosting & Security Products Knowledge: Solid understanding of SSL/TLS certificates (DV/OV/EV, validation, CA/B Forum requirements and lifecycle changes), email hosting and anti-spam, and Plesk licensing and hosting control panels.

Supplier & Vendor Management: Negotiates commercial terms, volume tiers, rebates and SLAs; runs business reviews; manages supplier performance, dependency and contract risk.

Commercial & P&L Acumen: Builds business cases; understands pricing, margin, unit economics, cannibalisation and reseller incentive models.

Product Strategy & Roadmapping: Translates strategy into operational roadmaps for the RCP and the SSL, email and Plesk product lines.

Project & Programme Management: Plans and delivers multi-party projects with Engineering and suppliers: scope, milestones, dependencies, risk logs and stakeholder updates, within a strong Agile/EOS rhythm.

Data & Funnel Analytics: Instruments and analyses order, provisioning and renewal journeys; separates price effects from product effects.

AI Proficiency: Embeds AI tools across daily work - discovery, documentation, analysis, supplier communication and GTM.

How we work at Openprovider

Self-management: you own your time, priorities and results, and raise issues early.

Learning Agility and AI Literacy: you learn fast and use AI with confidence and good judgement.

Adaptive Innovation Mindset: you see change as a chance to improve and help others move forward positively.

Quality Orientation: you take pride in your work, test assumptions with facts and deliver results others can rely on.

Customer Focus: you understand who your work serves, including our resellers, and make decisions that create real value for them.

What we offer

100% remote work (you can work from any location, no need to go to the office);

Paid time off and sick leave;

International team and regular online and offline events to stay connected;

Internal workshops, and knowledge-sharing sessions;

Quarterly review and annual salary review;

Flexible working hours;

We are an ISO 27001-certified remote workplace;

Meaningful work with real ownership and room to stretch beyond your comfort zone;

Courses in the Openprovider Academy, a structured onboarding path and a clear Career Framework to manage your own growth;

A Virtual Office that makes it easy to connect with colleagues, wherever you are.

Openprovider is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome all qualified candidates to apply.

About us

Most resellers spend too much money and time on domains. With Openprovider and our Membership program, you can buy, renew, and transfer domains at cost price on one platform to become a more successful and profitable reseller.

We are a rapidly-growing, ICANN-accredited domain registrar and technology scale-up founded in 2004 in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. We understand the frustrations of wasting hours searching for new domains at fair prices; being hit by unexpected renewal costs after the first year; and losing customers because you can’t offer attractive bundles.

That’s why we built a platform to easily manage operations for over 1,900 domain extensions. We were the first to offer a Membership Program to get the domains you need at cost price, and we've been helping clients sell millions of domains for more than 20 years.

We have been fully remote since 2020, and our team has only expanded since then. Our team currently consists of 90+ employees, who are spread across 20+ different countries and 4 different continents. We are proud of our fun and diverse team and regularly connect with each other through online and offline events.

Some careers open more doors than others.

Our products and services include advisory, financing, prime services, research and analysis, securities services, trading and sales and transaction banking.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join the Global Payment Services (GPS), GPS INM Product team as Product Manager – Receivables.

Job Introduction

Manage the GPS INM receivables portfolio, encompassing UPI, NACH, Virtual Accounts, Omni Collect and structured B2B reconciliation products, including DART, ARR and third-party offerings. The role covers the end-to-end product lifecycle, from concept, development and enhancement to launch, maintenance and commercialisation. Working under the guidance of the Senior Product Manager, coordinate internal teams and external partners to deliver seamless client onboarding, effective collection and reconciliation solutions, robust supporting processes, sound product governance and a consistent client experience.

Principal Responsibilities

Manage the development, enhancement, launch, maintenance and ongoing performance of UPI, NACH, Virtual Accounts, Omni Collect, DART, ARR and other structured B2B and third-party reconciliation offerings.
Translate client needs and business requirements into defined product designs, prioritised enhancements and actionable launch plans. Use market insights, competitor benchmarking and client feedback from Sales, Coverage and GPS teams to develop differentiated propositions, maintain a prioritised backlog and incorporate client validation and pilot feedback.
Evaluate partnerships with acquiring providers, payment platforms and reconciliation solution providers. Coordinate IT, Operations, Client Management, GPS teams and external partners to deliver integrated client collection and reconciliation propositions, with clear ownership, agreed actions and appropriate partner due diligence and governance.
Define and maintain end-to-end operating and service models covering client onboarding, production service continuity, collections, reconciliation, exception handling and ongoing servicing. Work with Operations and Client Management to document and agree workflows and resolve exceptions within agreed service timelines.
Coordinate product deployments, enhancements, testing and launch readiness, with documented requirements and stakeholder approvals. Deliver assigned initiatives against agreed milestones and provide concise updates on priorities, progress, risks and decisions, escalating delivery dependencies promptly to the Senior Product Manager.
Support commercialisation and client adoption through product collateral, sales enablement and ongoing enhancements. Partner with GPS and Coverage teams to convert client opportunities into suitable receivables solutions, tracking progress against agreed plans, product adoption and client usage.
Ensure alignment with applicable regulatory guidelines and HSBC policies, internal controls and the Group Compliance Policy. Identify product, third-party and operational risks with risk stewards, coordinate controls and approvals, track mitigating actions and report losses appropriately. Support third-party assessments, regulatory reporting and client-issue resolution; monitor relevant collection, reconciliation and applicable partner chargeback/refund metrics; submit credit-risk exceptions and pricing decisions for approval; and ensure timely implementation of audit actions and resolution of regulator-raised issues.

Role Requirements / Education Qualifications / Certifications / Experience:

Graduate or postgraduate qualification, or equivalent, with a university degree and/or relevant training qualifications.
Demonstrated progressive experience and a proven track record in cash management, receivables and/or payments product development and management, or equivalent relevant experience, including product development, project management, fintech engagement and market- or client-facing banking functions.
Corporate transaction banking or cash management experience is preferred, but not mandatory. Experience in merchant acquiring, UPI collections, NACH, Virtual Accounts or structured B2B reconciliation is preferred, but not mandatory; familiarity with DART, ARR or third-party reconciliation offerings is beneficial.
Demonstrated project and programme management experience, including co-creating solutions with IT and internal business partners. Excellent planning, organisation and time-management skills, with the ability to influence decisions and deliver within tight deadlines.
Ability to develop innovative, flexible solutions addressing client needs and to understand clients’ business models, operating needs and core business fundamentals. Sound business acumen and commercial awareness, including relevant economic, cultural, procedural and regulatory considerations.
Strong interpersonal, negotiation and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build effective internal and external relationships. A collaborative approach to teamwork, supported by self-motivation and a proactive working style.
Strong numerical and analytical skills, with the ability to develop well-founded recommendations for decision-making. Familiarity with emerging technologies is preferred.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including clear, compelling presentations. Fluency in English is expected; additional language skills are beneficial.

Pro-tip : Familiarity with AI-enabled tools is an advantage.

Additional Notes:

Mandatory to successfully complete Anti-Money Laundering and Sanctions training and post-course assessment, as required.

As an employee, you are required to perform your duties in a professional capacity exercising independent judgement, discretion and decision-making authority in planning, organising, directing work, supervising and appraising the work of team members, as applicable; and taking accountability for delivery outcomes. You will represent the organization with relevant internal and external stakeholders. You will allocate and prioritize work, provide direction and feedback, manage team capacity and leave in line with policy as applicable.

You’ll achieve more at HSBC.

HSBC is committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and opportunities to grow within an inclusive and diverse environment.

Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.

Description:

VP

Experience

6+ years

Role: Senior Product Manager

Grow the subscription people are glad they pay for.

With millions of active users across the Microsoft 365 ecosystem and Copilot usage growing fast, consumer subscriptions are one of the largest surfaces anywhere to shape the next chapter of Microsoft's subscription business. Copilot is making Microsoft 365 more powerful every month, and that creates a rare opportunity: help more people subscribe, help subscribers discover the plan that fits them best, and invent new ways to pay for AI as it becomes part of everyday life. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own consumer monetization on mobile, a business with enormous reach where the playbook for AI subscriptions is still being written.

Why this role, why now

Copilot recently came together as one app across web, desktop and mobile, and AI is reshaping what people expect from a subscription. Plans now range from core productivity to Copilot-powered and Pro experiences, and usage-based offers are opening entirely new business models. Early signals on mobile are solid, and in-app purchase is live across iOS and Android. This is the moment to define what a world-class AI subscription business looks like.

How we work

Small, empowered mission teams with clear ownership.
Every bet starts with a written hypothesis, is measured rigorously, and decisions are made on evidence.
AI-native by default: we use AI agents and tools throughout our own workflow to research, prototype, analyze and ship faster.
Ship fast, learn faster, scale what works.
We earn the upgrade; we never trap people in a subscription.
India shapes global strategy here, not just execution.

You'll thrive here if...

You treat a paywall as a product and can explain why one trial converts and another does not.
You are excited by inventing new ways to pay for AI, from premium tiers to usage-based packs.
You form a view on why people pay, and change it quickly when the data disagrees.
App store policies energize your creativity rather than limit it.
You think in lifetime value, not just conversion, and are as comfortable modelling unit economics with finance as sketching a flow with a designer.
You already prototype, analyze and write with AI, and want a team that expects it.

This role may not be for you if...

You want a defined backlog handed to you.
You measure success by features shipped rather than customers who pay and stay.
Dark patterns tempt you.

Why join us

Few roles let you shape how millions of people experience and pay for AI in their daily lives. You will own a global subscription business across growth, economics, upgrades and new business models, with the freedom to set direction and a fast-moving, AI-native team beside you. If that excites you, we would love to meet you.

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities

What you will own

You own a revenue-bearing business end to end across four connected levers: subscriber growth, unit economics, upgrades and new business models. Senior here means you set the strategy and experiment roadmap across all four, navigate real platform constraints and align partners you don't manage.

Grow subscriptions: attract and convert new Microsoft 365 subscribers on mobile through great paywalls, trials and purchase experiences on the App Store and Google Play.
Improve unit economics: raise lifetime value and ARPU through smarter packaging, pricing and offers, and by keeping subscribers engaged and renewing.
Lead upgrades: design upgrade experiences that help subscribers discover Copilot-powered and Pro plans at the moment the value is obvious.
Build new business models: launch and scale consumption packs and other usage-based offers that let people buy more AI exactly when they need it.

You will move the metrics that define a healthy subscription business: paid subscriber growth, trial conversion, upgrade rate, ARPU, lifetime value, retention and consumption revenue.

POSITION PURPOSE:

The Principal Product Manager is responsible for the overall product vision, strategy and roadmap across a specific Platform or domain and works on the hardest problems within the Platform. They make specific contributions to Product and Platform delivery by working directly with Product Squads within the Platform to ensure each product is oriented toward business outcomes that improve company performance. The Principal Product Manager partners directly with the Platform Lead and their teams to deliver. The Principal Product Manager is an expert communicator that represents the Platform by presenting to senior leaders across Bayer and externally to accelerate digital transformation and build Bayer’s reputation as a digital leading company.

Principal Product Managers apply the product management discipline to some of the hardest problems within the Platform. They ensure that products are fulfilling their primary purpose to enable users to perform tasks that create value for the company by:

-Setting strategic vision for the product to ensure the customer and their needs are at the center; and ensuring team priorities are supporting business outcomes for customer, product, technical and enabling teams. This requires continual alignment of the product strategy and objectives with customer, product, technical, and enabling teams

-Managing the product backlog, which prioritizes the work of the assigned squads, to achieve the vision and aligned strategy.

To successfully manage these areas of responsibility, Principal Product Managers must have a deep understanding of the product domain, related technology, and architecture.

YOUR TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Product Management

The product manager is accountable for the overall success of a product throughout its lifecycle, from conception to decommissioning. They identify domain needs, develop, and validate product concepts, and build a business case. They oversee the product's build and launch, including any sourced services; as well as ensure product availability, stability, and compliance needs are met. Product managers collaborate with various teams, including product development, marketing, finance, legal, manufacturing, operations, and sales, as needed, to ensure cohesive progress and success.

Product Managers drive agile best practices with the team to improve delivery, including continuous planning ahead of each development cycle (e.g. sprint planning) and working together to co-create user stories aligned with the product backlog prioritization. In addition to guiding the team product managers have duties like market opportunity identification, competitive analysis, sales enablement, or monitoring domain performance.

Stakeholder Engagement

It is vital for the product manager to identify their key stakeholder group. Though many strong and loud opinions will be expressed, an effective product manager uses discretion to deliver their product in a way that meets the needs of users and stakeholders who will ensure value is realized for Bayer. Stakeholders should trust that the product manager not only understands their needs but will actively work to ensure their needs are met while delivering the product.

Product Strategy

The product manager must provide strategic leadership with full end-to-end ownership for their assigned products throughout the entire product lifecycle. They are responsible for planning and optimizing capabilities to deliver business outcomes in the most efficient way. Product managers require strong strategic planning, decision making, and influencing skills to balance the needs of users and various stakeholders.

Product Discovery & Delivery

The product manager is responsible for creating comprehensive product roadmaps, to clarify user needs and non-functional requirements. They provide product oversight by tracking and reporting progress against 90-day outcomes and overall product health (including budget responsibilities). They also plan and manage product delivery while streamlining the corresponding backlog. Product managers are responsible for monitoring user feedback and metrics to co-create solutions that drive a better user experience and deliver more business value. They leverage Design Thinking methodology starting with user needs to prioritize problems and through discovery they perform usability, feasibility, business fit and value testing to determine the optimal solution.

People & Collaboration

Product managers must proactively communicate and collaborate with product users and stakeholders, which requires strong strategic communication skills. Effective cross-functional collaboration is critical for product managers, bringing together diverse skills and knowledge to deliver a valuable product. It's important to maintain strong and productive working relationships with colleagues in product management, engineering, and other technically focused organizations. The Principal Product Manager serves as a Product Management Chapter Lead for their Platform, where they are responsible for development of the product management community to improve product management and agile practices, fostering a culture of excellence, collaboration, and continuous learning.

Provide customer, market, partner, and delivery insights to product leadership to help shape the broader integrations strategy and roadmap.

Gather, validate, and translate customer, partner, commercial, and internal stakeholder needs into clear product requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and prioritized backlog items.

DESCRIPTION

Are you passionate about building innovative, customer facing analytics products that help businesses make smarter purchasing decisions? Do you enjoy solving complex customer problems at scale using data, analytics, and artificial intelligence? Are you excited about shaping how organizations of all sizes understand, manage, and optimize their business spending?

Amazon Business is transforming how businesses, governments, and organizations purchase products and manage procurement operations. Serving millions of business customers worldwide, Amazon Business combines the selection, convenience, and value of Amazon with capabilities tailored to the unique needs of business customers.

Amazon Business Analytics (ABA) plays a critical role in this transformation by building a suite of customer facing analytics products that help organizations turn purchasing data into actionable insights. Our customers range from small and medium businesses to large enterprises and public sector organizations. Our products empower procurement leaders, finance teams, and business administrators to understand organizational spending, identify savings opportunities, monitor purchasing behavior, and make informed business decisions.

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager, Technical (PMT) to help shape and deliver the next generation of Amazon Business Analytics experiences. In this role, you will drive product strategy and execution across our customer facing analytics portfolio, spanning spend visibility, self service reporting, intelligent insights, and AI powered conversational analytics. You will build intuitive and scalable products for the full range of business customers, from those seeking simple, out of the box spending insights to large enterprises requiring sophisticated analytics across complex organizational structures.

You will have the opportunity to reimagine how business customers interact with their purchasing data, moving beyond traditional dashboards and reports toward intelligent, proactive, and conversational experiences. You will use advances in generative AI, large language models, and modern data technologies to make analytics more accessible, personalized, and actionable for customers worldwide.

This is a highly visible role that requires strong customer obsession, technical judgment, strategic thinking, and the ability to influence and deliver across multiple engineering and business organizations. The ideal candidate thrives in ambiguity, dives deep into customer and technical challenges, and has a demonstrated track record of building and scaling customer facing technology products.

We are open to hiring candidates to work from the following locations: Hyderabad, IND | Bangalore, IND

Key job responsibilities
As the PMT for ABA, you will own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for customer facing analytics capabilities across Amazon Business. You will develop a deep understanding of how small businesses, large enterprises, procurement professionals, and finance teams use purchasing data, and turn those needs into intuitive, scalable, and differentiated product experiences.

You will lead the development of intelligent analytics experiences, including conversational interfaces, natural language querying, proactive insights, and AI powered capabilities. You will also build products that help customers analyze organizational spending, identify savings opportunities, and improve procurement outcomes. You will balance ease of use for smaller businesses with the depth that large enterprises require, and develop capabilities that serve customers across multiple geographies.

You will partner closely with engineering, applied science, UX, and data teams to define product requirements, evaluate architectural tradeoffs, and deliver scalable, reliable analytics solutions. You will define success metrics and use customer feedback, experimentation, and data to keep improving outcomes. Finally, you will collaborate with senior leaders across Amazon Business to align priorities and drive decisions.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor's degree
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience in building and driving adoption of new tools
- Experience in using analytical tools, such as Tableau, Qlikview, QuickSight
- Experience in an operational environment developing, fast-prototyping, piloting and launching analytic products

Forward Deployed Domain Practitioners (FDDPs) – Healthcare Domain

Converge for Healthcare | Deloitte Consulting

About the Role

The Team

This role sits within Converge for Healthcare, Deloitte's industry-focused asset studio for healthcare, part of Deloitte Consulting's Innovation & Delivery Transformation (I&DT) practice. I&DT brings an engineering- and innovation-led mindset to how Deloitte builds, delivers, and scales technology-enabled solutions.

Data Studio is Converge for Healthcare's foundational platform—combining agentic AI and analytics capabilities atop a unified healthcare data foundation to turn healthcare data into decision-ready insight and automated action across the Converge for Healthcare product portfolio.

Forward Deployed Domain Practitioners are the business and domain half of Converge for Healthcare's Forward Deployed model. Where Product Forward Deployed Engineers (pFDEs) cover product and technology, FDDPs cover business and domain—partnering with pFDEs, client account teams, and product teams to define the real client problem, prove measurable value, and identify where the platform can deliver more, feeding real-world domain learnings back into the platform roadmap.

Position Summary

As a Forward Deployed Domain Practitioner within Converge for Healthcare, you will work directly with clients, Deloitte Consulting's broader Health Care consulting practice, and Converge Health's product and engineering teams. Paired with a pFDE on each engagement, you'll bring the client-domain fluency that shapes what gets built on Data Studio and why—defining the business problem and success criteria, aligning client stakeholders on what value means, and translating real operational workflows into the requirements, rules, and edge cases the pFDE builds against.

This is a domain-led, business-facing role grounded in production reality rather than abstract requirements. You'll work alongside real users, real workflows, and real data, on engagements that are scoped, time-boxed, and exit-oriented—leaving behind documented domain artifacts and reusable patterns so that each deployment makes the next one materially faster.

The role draws on healthcare breadth rather than a single specialty, spanning provider and payer domains—from revenue cycle, utilization management, and clinical operations to network strategy, risk adjustment, actuarial, and beyond.

Key Responsibilities

Work You'll Do

• Presales & opportunity shaping: Partner with Health Care consulting teams, account teams, and pFDEs during the sales cycle—leading business discovery, mapping current-state workflows, and building the value hypothesis and business case, while the pFDE leads technical discovery and demonstrations, to qualify client needs into Product fit or out to Services as custom scope.

• Business problem definition & success criteria: Frame each use case around a concrete operational problem, establish baseline performance, and define measurable outcomes the client and Deloitte agree on (e.g., denial rates, days in A/R, prior authorization turnaround, coding accuracy, care-gap closure).

• Domain-to-build translation: Translate business needs into the workflow logic, decision rules, policy references, exceptions, and acceptance criteria the pFDE builds against—and contribute domain-accurate, labelled test cases to the use case's evaluation set so agent outputs are judged against how the work is actually done.

• Use case discovery beyond the original ask: Surface adjacent, domain-specific use cases grounded in what you observe in the client's workflows and data, size their value, and route them through engagement governance and the product roadmap—never through informal commitments on features or timelines.

• Stakeholder alignment & adoption: Build alignment among client executives, operational leaders, and front-line users on what value means for the engagement, and lead the process change, training, and adoption activities that turn a working capability into one people actually use.

• Value realization & measurement: Stay engaged post-launch to track outcomes against the agreed baseline, diagnose where value is or isn't landing, and develop the evidence and client value stories that support adoption, renewal, and platform growth.

• Field-to-product feedback & reusable domain assets: Capture recurring domain patterns, workflow variations, and policy or regulatory shifts, translate them into concrete use-case and capability requests for Product Managers, and codify them into reusable domain playbooks, value frameworks, and use-case definitions for the next client.

Qualifications

Required

• 8+ years of experience in healthcare consulting, provider or payer operations, or a domain-specialist role in healthcare technology

• 4+ years of client-facing experience leading business discovery, process redesign, or business case development

• Comfortable client-facing, including product demos and discovery with senior stakeholders

• Based in India, able to work virtually with US stakeholders on US-market direction and its nuances

Preferred

• Master's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Public Health, Health Informatics, Nursing or another clinical discipline, such as an MBA, MHA, or MPH, or another relevant advanced degree

• Relevant professional credentials (e.g., HFMA CRCR or CHFP, AAPC or AHIMA coding certifications, clinical licensure such as RN, or SOA actuarial credentials)

• Experience with AI, automation, or advanced analytics implementations in a healthcare setting

• Experience in product- or platform-based delivery models, as distinct from purely services-based delivery

Core Competencies

• Domain-first profile—deep healthcare business and operational expertise paired with enough technical fluency to partner credibly with engineers on agentic AI and data solutions

• Strong healthcare domain knowledge spanning provider and/or payer domains—such as revenue cycle, utilization management, care management, clinical operations, network strategy, risk adjustment, or actuarial—with the versatility to apply it across multiple areas rather than a single specialty

• Proven ability to diagnose operational workflows, quantify improvement opportunities, and build credible business cases and ROI models that client executives act on

• Practical understanding of what agentic AI can and cannot do reliably—human-in-the-loop design, accuracy-versus-automation trade-offs, and how to judge agent outputs for domain correctness—without needing to write code

• Working knowledge of healthcare data and data standards (e.g., claims, remittances, EMR data, X12 EDI, HL7, FHIR) at a business level—what the data means, where it breaks, and how data quality affects business outcomes

• Fluency in the regulatory and policy landscape that shapes healthcare workflows—such as CMS rules, payer medical and reimbursement policies, coding standards (ICD-10, CPT, HCPCS), prior authorization requirements, and HIPAA

• Strong requirements and process skills—process mapping, decision tables, use-case definition, and acceptance criteria that engineers can build and test against

• Judgment to size each engagement—recognizing when a client problem maps to a proven use case, when it needs meaningful extension, and when it is custom scope better served by Services

• Commercial instinct grounded in client value—spotting where the platform can do more for a client and framing it in outcome terms, while respecting engagement governance and the product roadmap

• Change management and adoption experience, including redesigning roles and workflows around automation and bringing front-line teams along

• Intellectual curiosity about how AI is changing the way healthcare work gets done, and a strong pull toward rethinking workflows rather than automating them as they are

Job Description:

Location: Bangalore

Experience: 3 to 6 years

About Nubra: Nubra is a trading platform for people who take trading seriously, whether they scalp index options on expiry day or run multi-leg strategies over weeks. We've built Smart Flexi Orders, multi-strike charts, tick-level option chain data, a multi-leg strategy builder, smart watchlists, automation APIs, and flexible collateral management, and we're still early in what we want the product to become.

Most of our users have tried other platforms before us. They know exactly what breaks at 9:15 AM, which order types are missing, and how many taps it takes to adjust a position when the market moves against them. Our job is to make those moments better. You can see the product at nubra.io.

The role: You'll own the roadmap for the parts of Nubra that traders use every single session: order placement and execution, the option chain, the strategy builder, charts, and our automation APIs. You'll work day to day with engineering and design, and closely with compliance and risk, since almost everything we ship has a regulatory angle. This is a hands-on role. You'll write the specs, sit in on technical discussions about latency and data feeds, look at the numbers yourself, and talk to traders every week.

Coming from e-commerce or D2C? We'd like to hear from you. Some of the best product thinking for a trading app comes from people who have built checkout flows, high-volume order systems, or products where a few seconds of delay costs real money. What we need from you is a genuine interest in markets and the willingness to get fluent in options and derivatives quickly. If you already trade on the side, even better.

What you'll be responsible for:

Roadmap and product direction:
Own the roadmap for order types, option chain, strategy builder, charts and automation APIs.
Decide what we build next and, just as often, what we don't. Be able to explain the reasoning to the team.
Keep a close eye on other trading and investing platforms in India and abroad, and know where we're ahead and where we're behind.
Building and shipping:
Turn trader workflows into clear specs that engineers can build from without a dozen follow-up calls.
Work with engineering on the trade-offs that matter in trading: speed, reliability, and accuracy of data under heavy market load.
Work with design so that complex features (multi-leg orders, margin, Greeks) feel simple to use.
Plan releases carefully. A bug in an order flow is not the same as a bug in a settings page.
Users and data:
Speak with active traders regularly through calls, support tickets, community channels and usage data.
Define what success looks like for each feature and track adoption, retention, order success rates and trading behaviour.
Run experiments where it makes sense and be honest about results when something doesn't work.
Compliance and risk:
Work with compliance and risk teams so that new features meet SEBI and exchange requirements from day one, not as an afterthought.
Understand how margin, collateral and risk checks affect the user experience, and design around them sensibly.


Your first six months, roughly:

Month 1: Use the product the way our users do, with real trades if you're comfortable. Read support tickets, sit with engineering, and get to know the order lifecycle end to end.
Months 2 to 3: Take ownership of one feature area and ship your first meaningful improvement. Set up the metrics you'll use to judge it.
Months 4 to 6: Own the roadmap for your area, with a clear view of priorities for the next two quarters and the user evidence to back them.


What we're looking for:

3 to 6 years of product management experience in trading, broking, fintech, capital markets, e-commerce or D2C.
You've shipped consumer products end to end, ideally ones with high transaction volumes, real-time flows or demanding power users.
You're comfortable with data. You can write or read a query, build a funnel, and tell the difference between a real trend and noise.
You understand trading concepts such as order types, options, derivatives and market data, or you're clearly on your way there.
You write clearly and can get engineering, design, compliance and business teams to agree on a plan.
You're interested in markets. Not as a line on your CV, but because you actually find them interesting.


Good to have:

Personal trading experience, especially in F&O.
Prior work at a broker, exchange or prop trading firm.
Experience with options or derivatives platforms specifically.
Working knowledge of SEBI regulations and NSE/BSE rules.
A background in analytics or quant, or experience with real-time data systems.
Experience building payments, checkout or other high-trust flows where conversion and reliability both matter.


How we work: We start with the user. Here that means thinking like a trader. If you can't explain why a trader would care, it probably doesn't belong on the roadmap. We move quickly. Markets change fast and so do our users' expectations. We'd rather ship, learn and fix than wait for a perfect version.

We use data, and we make calls. Numbers inform our decisions, but we don't hide behind them. Sometimes you have to back your judgement. We own outcomes. Shipping a feature isn't the finish line. Whether it helped traders is what counts.

What you get:

Ownership of the core of a trading product used by active traders every market day.
Problems that are genuinely hard: real-time data, complex instruments, regulation and user experience all in one place.
A small, capable team where your work is visible and your opinion counts.
A steep learning curve in capital markets, if you're new to the space.
Competitive pay with performance-based incentives.

jobs.sourceTitle: Senior Principal - Design Assurance & Product Management - Portfolio-wide Analytics
jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
GSK remains committed to achieving bold commercial ambitions for the future. By 2031, we aim to deliver £40 billion in annual sales, leveraging our existing strong performance momentum to significantly increase our positive impact on the health of billions of patients globally. Our Ahead Together strategy is centred on early intervention to prevent and alter the course of disease, thereby protecting people and supporting healthcare systems.

Our diverse portfolio consists of vaccines, specialty medicines, and general medicines.

Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges.

Domain focus: Portfolio-wide analytics supporting all domain product owners.

Job Purpose:

Own portfolio intelligence and investment analytics for Cyber Architecture and Solutions. You turn portfolio, vendor and delivery data into the evidence prioritisation and investment decisions are made from, and you are the analytical backbone of the function.

About the team:

Design Assurance and Product Management makes sure security is designed in before anything is built, and that GSK's security capabilities are run as products rather than projects. Design Assurance independently verifies that solutions meet the architecture standards set elsewhere in Cyber Architecture and Solutions; it writes none of those standards, and that separation is what makes the review worth anything. Product Management owns the security portfolio, vendor governance and investment analytics, and is how GSK manages its managed service vendor as a whole. Platform support engineering moves into this function, with a small internal team retaining oversight while the vendor operates more than 30 platforms and the data fabric under an OTO model. Seventeen roles.

What makes this role different. A genuinely analytical role, not a reporting role, and the distinction matters. Producing the pack is the easy part; the value is spotting the trend nobody asked about and bringing it to leadership unprompted. You do not need to have built security controls, but you do need to read a MITRE ATT&CK coverage map and judge for yourself whether two tools genuinely overlap or only appear to in the licence schedule. Your numbers will be used in investment decisions and challenged by people who do not want the answer, so they have to reconcile and you have to defend them.

Key responsibilities:

This role will provide you the opportunity to lead key activities to progress your career. These responsibilities include some of the following:

Own portfolio intelligence across the Cyber Architecture and Solutions product and project estate.
Build and maintain the investment analytics that prioritisation decisions are made from.
Produce portfolio reporting the leadership team steers by, and make the numbers defensible under challenge.
Analyse vendor spend, performance and value across the managed service, including the OTO transition.
Model investment scenarios and quantify trade-offs between competing priorities.
Track benefit realisation against the cases that funded the work, including where benefits did not materialise.
Own the data and definitions behind the reporting so figures reconcile across every forum.
Identify trends and outliers and bring them to leadership attention unprompted.
Build the costed option set for the annual plan, sequencing investment and decommission against the renewal calendar so consolidation savings are realised in the year they are claimed.
Set the analytical standard for the function — data lineage, definition control and reproducibility — so any figure in a leadership pack can be traced to source and re-derived by someone else.
Lead your team in using approved AI tools to improve productivity and ways of working, role-modelling responsible use and follow GSK's Responsible AI, privacy and security requirements.
Apply data integrity and GxP record-keeping expectations to the figures this role publishes, so portfolio and benefit reporting stands up to audit.

Basic Qualifications:

15+ years in cyber security or technology portfolio analytics in a regulated environment — domain focus: portfolio-wide analytics supporting all domain product owners
Building a security portfolio intelligence capability at enterprise scale — threat-to-tool coverage matrix showing weak, duplicated or missing coverage, investment gaps and decommission candidates
Automated portfolio monitoring — integrating tool inventory, licence and consumption, contract and renewal, cost and risk data into continuously refreshed dashboards, reconciling incomplete CMDB data
Evidence-based decommission and consolidation business cases with quantified savings or risk reduction, analysed on the same domain structure as Security Solution Engineering
Applying AI and machine learning to portfolio analytics — anomaly detection on licence and cost data, AI-assisted coverage mapping and assessment of AI-enabled security tools

Preferred Qualifications:

Power BI or equivalent, SQL and Python for portfolio analytics, automation and data engineering
Security tool landscape knowledge across all security product domains, enough to judge whether two tools genuinely overlap
MITRE ATT&CK and NIST CSF applied to coverage mapping rather than cited in isolation
Total cost of ownership, licence utilisation and shelf-ware analysis, including unused entitlement ahead of renewal
Investment modelling and analytics support for domain product managers' portfolio decisions
Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
Typical tools and technologies: Power BI or equivalent, SQL and Python for analytics and automation, data modelling across tool inventory, licence entitlement and consumption, contract and renewal dates and cost, threat-to-tool coverage mapping using MITRE ATT&CK and NIST CSF, total cost of ownership and shelf-ware analysis, ServiceNow and CMDB data extraction, automated portfolio monitoring.

Skills

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. Pepper is an agentic organic growth platform. We get brands recommended and bought across humans and AI agents, from discoverability to revenue.

Our bet.

Search is now an answer, and increasingly an action an agent takes for a person.
Every brand has three kinds of visitors: humans who search and buy, crawlers that index, and agents that discover, compare, and transact.
We are building the Organic Growth OS for all three that drives enterprise first outcomes
The winners of the next decade will be the brands that machines understand, trust, recommend, and can act on.

Agentic commerce.

A new buyer has arrived, and it is not human: AI agents research, compare, add to cart, check out, and book for customers.
Winning it means being legible to agents: discoverable in AI answers, readable at the catalog and pricing level, verifiable by identity, and able to transact.
Most brands are invisible or unusable to agents today.
We close that gap, and prove it with attribution from recommendation to agent action to revenue.

The role.

A seat for an entrepreneur, not a hire to run an existing machine.
Own Atlas and the platform around it end to end: product, architecture, and applied AI in one mandate.
The prize is US mid-market and enterprise growth.

Platform-led operations.

Pepper is moving from an AI-enabled services business that delivers with people to a platform first business that delivers with agents. You own that transition.
Today human teams run much of the client work: audits, briefs, technical fixes, content operations, and reporting.
The shift: move delivery onto Atlas so agents execute, while humans move up to strategy, judgment, creative direction, and client relationships.
The principle: agents drive delivery, humans augment strategy on top.
Decompose the services playbook into deterministic tasks and agent workflows, and automate the delivery layer end to end.
Instrument it with monitors and evals so quality holds without a person checking every output.
Redesign how the company is organized around the platform, not headcount.

You will:

Own the Atlas roadmap and agent architecture, deciding where LLMs beat deterministic code.
Grow the automation surface and raise the share of work done with no human in the loop.
Own agent readiness, identity, and commerce so agents can discover, trust, and buy.
Run the monitors, evals, and guardrails that make autonomous output reliable enough to sell on outcomes.
Build and scale the product, engineering, and AI teams, and tie the roadmap to ARR and margin.
Convert Pepper's services delivery into platform-led agent workflows, retiring manual steps so agents execute and strategists direct.

Who you are.

A founder or founding engineer who has taken something from zero and wants to build again.
Has scaled product and engineering teams through real growth.
Has shipped agentic systems to production, not demos, and knows when to use LLMs versus deterministic code.
Has built for US mid-market and enterprise buyers and their reliability and security bar.
Combined product and technology fluency. SEO, GEO, or MarTech experience is a plus.
Has turned a manual operation into a product or platform, and wants to do it at Pepper's scale.
