jobs.sourceTitle: Director, Product Management — Core Database Engine & AI
jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
Our Company

At Teradata, we believe that people thrive when empowered with better information. Teradata Autonomous Knowledge Platform activates enterprise intelligence by unifying data, knowledge and business context to achieve tangible outcomes. With Teradata, organizations can provide agents with full context for impact when it matters. Our solution lets businesses connect and scale on premises, in the cloud, or through a hybrid approach. Teradata delivers real business value with AI. 

What You'll Do

In this role, you will lead product strategy and execution for Teradata's core database engine: the massively parallel query engine behind every workload on the platform. You will shape the roadmap across the optimizer, execution runtime, workload management, and Global Planner, and own how the engine performs on native storage, cloud object storage, and open table formats such as Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake. 

This role sits at the intersection of the database engine and AI. AI agents are becoming the dominant consumers of enterprise data, issuing high volumes of exploratory, speculative queries, while GenAI and machine learning can improve the engine from the inside. Every core component needs to be rethought in this light, and you will lead that rethink and turn it into a roadmap engineering can build. 

Two things anchor the role. Performance: you will spend significant time inside real workloads, query plans, and benchmarks, working with engineering to deliver measurable gains release after release. SQL: you will be the steward of Teradata SQL, the surface customers live in, making its syntax, semantics, and ergonomics simpler, more expressive, and safer for developers, analysts, and AI agents. 

Strategy: Own the engine vision and multi-year roadmap, co-owning architecture direction with senior engineering leaders and making principled trade-offs across performance, cost, and complexity. 
AI and agents: Lead the rethink of every core engine component for AI agents as the new dominant workload, and apply GenAI and ML inside the engine to make it faster and more autonomous. 
Optimizer, execution, and workload management: Agents send many redundant queries. Explore optimizing across queries, sharing intermediate results, and returning early or approximate answers. Apply learned cardinality and cost models and LLM-assisted rewrite, with guardrails that protect plan stability. Define how workload management absorbs bursty machine traffic through agent identity, priorities, and budgets. 
Performance: Work hands-on with engineering on query plans, regressions, and bottlenecks. Own the benchmark suite and KPIs (latency, concurrency, plan stability, price-performance), including agentic workloads, and build regression gates into releases. 
Open Table formats: Own the engine side of Iceberg and Delta Lake (scan planning, pruning, pushdown, write paths) so customers never trade performance for openness. Automate statistics, clustering, and compaction with AI. 
SQL language and query interface: Design features that turn complex problems into simple, readable queries, reduce footguns while keeping power and backward compatibility, and stay aligned with ANSI SQL. Make the dialect something agents can safely generate and execute, and let agents steer with cost estimates, plan explanations, and hints. 

Who You'll Work With

You will work with senior database engineering leaders, performance engineering, AI platform teams, the open table format product team, sales engineering, and executive leadership across the US, Europe, and India. This role starts as an individual contributor, leading through technical depth and influence and mentoring Staff-level PMs. It may grow into managing a team of product managers. 

What Makes You a Qualified Candidate

15+ years in databases, query engines, or distributed data systems, including senior product management or equivalent principal or staff engineering experience 
Expert understanding of database internals: query planning, cost-based optimization, execution models, and MPP trade-offs 
Deep SQL expertise: a heavy SQL user (data engineer, analyst, or DBA) with strong opinions on language design, ergonomics, and compatibility 
A hands-on performance mindset: reading query plans, designing benchmarks, and finding root causes with senior engineers 
A strong working understanding of LLMs and AI agents, and an informed view on how they change database design and how ML can improve database internals 
Architecture-level knowledge of Snowflake, Databricks, and ClickHouse, and fluency in lakehouse architecture and open table formats 
Degree in Computer Science or a related field; an MS or PhD in databases, distributed systems, or ML for systems is a plus 

What You'll Bring

First-principles thinking and good taste: willingness to question long-standing database assumptions, a preference for elegance over verbosity, customer obsession, daily use of GenAI tools, and the credibility to earn the trust of senior engineers 
The ability to read research critically, separate promise from hype, and design experiments to prove value, with a track record of setting multi-year platform strategy 
A plus: experience designing SQL features or language extensions, hands-on work with optimizers or learned database components, open-source contributions, or publications at SIGMOD, VLDB, or CIDR

Position Overview

The Experienced Product Owner is an experienced, functionally deep Workday professional who owns one or more Workday modules end-to-end on behalf of Revantage and its PortCos. This is not a passive coordination role — it is an active, hands-on domain mastery role. You are the subject-matter expert, the decision-maker, the stakeholder champion, and the product strategist for your assigned module(s). You will work across a complex multi-PortCo environment, running user forums, managing the release roadmap, driving adoption, and continuously finding ways to extract more value from the platform. This role focuses on the US Payroll & Benefits Module. Additional module expertise is a plus.

Key Responsibilities

Domain Ownership & Functional Mastery

Own your assigned Workday module(s): US Payroll & Benefits end-to-end — from strategy and design through configuration, testing, deployment, and ongoing optimization.
Develop and maintain deep functional expertise in your domain(s), staying current with Workday product updates, roadmap changes, and community best practices.
Serve as the primary point of contact and escalation resource for your module area across all PortCos.
Maintain comprehensive knowledge of how your module(s) interact with upstream and downstream systems and processes — and design solutions with those dependencies in mind.
Think beyond Workday: identify complementary or supplementary technologies that could enhance capability in your domain — whether that is AI-powered tools, third-party integrations, or adjacent platforms.

PortCo Engagement & Stakeholder Management

Build and maintain strong relationships with HR leaders, operations teams, and business stakeholders across multiple PortCos.
Act as a trusted advisor — understanding each PortCo's unique workforce model, business context, and HR priorities.
Run structured Product Owner forums, working groups, and user communities to surface requirements, share updates, and drive alignment.
Manage competing priorities across PortCos with transparency — communicating trade-offs, timelines, and decisions clearly to all stakeholders.
Facilitate requirements workshops and design sessions, translating business needs into clear, actionable Workday solutions.

Roadmap & Release Ownership

Own and maintain the product roadmap for your module(s) — balancing strategic enhancements, PortCo-driven requirements, bug fixes, and Workday release adoption.
Evaluate every Workday bi-annual release for impact and opportunity within your domain — leading opt-in decisions, testing, and rollout planning.
Prioritize the backlog in collaboration with stakeholders, the Functional Architect, and People Technology leadership.
Ensure all enhancements are delivered with appropriate change management, training, and communications to end users and HR teams.
Track and report on the delivery and benefit realization of roadmap initiatives.

Hands-On Delivery

Remain hands-on with Workday configuration in your module area — able to configure, test, validate and deploy. 
Lead user acceptance testing (UAT) for enhancements and releases within your domain.
Create design documents, configuration specifications, and test plans before deployment.
Own day-to-day delivery.

Ecosystem & Innovation Thinking

Continuously evaluate the HR technology landscape for innovations relevant to your module area — e.g., AI in recruiting, manager effectiveness tools, payroll analytics.
Propose and build the business case for technology enhancements or new tool adoption where Workday alone does not fully meet business needs.
Collaborate with vendors (Workday, Paradox, HiredScore, Peakon, etc.) to stay ahead of product developments and advocate for Revantage's priorities.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of Workday functional experience with deep, hands-on expertise in at least two Workday modules.
Demonstrated experience owning a Workday module in a production environment — including enhancements, releases, stakeholder management, and roadmap ownership.
Nice to have experience working in a multi-entity, multi-PortCo, or shared-services HR technology model.
Strong understanding of Workday business process configuration, security roles, reporting, and calculated fields.
Proven ability to engage and influence senior HR stakeholders without direct authority.
Experience running forums, steering committees, or user communities across a distributed stakeholder base.
Global Workday implementation or support experience — able to navigate multi-jurisdiction complexity.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills — able to translate technical concepts for business audiences and vice versa.

Module-specific Experience

US Payroll

Payroll processing, tax configuration, and compliance — configuration and operational support.

Payroll Processing: Pay group setup, payroll calendars, run categories, gross-to-net calculation, and on/off-cycle run management.
Earnings & Deductions: Earning codes, deduction codes, arrears handling, garnishments, and pay component mapping from time and compensation.
Tax Configuration: Federal, state, and local tax setup, reciprocity rules, tax withholding elections, and year-end W-2 processing.
Compliance: ACA reporting, FLSA overtime, pay equity audits, and regulatory filing support.
Integrations & Reporting: GL mapping, bank file generation, payroll reconciliation, and audit-ready payroll registers.

US Benefits

Benefit plan configuration, open enrollment, and compliance — configuration and operational support.

Plan Configuration: Medical, dental, vision, FSA/HSA, life, disability, and voluntary benefit plan setup including carrier connections.
Eligibility & Enrollment: Eligibility rules, dependent coverage, qualifying life events, passive and active enrollment configuration.
Open Enrollment: OE event setup, employee self-service configuration, enrollment windows, and communication triggers.
ACA Compliance: 1095-C configuration, measurement periods, affordability calculations, and IRS filing support.
Integrations & Reporting: Benefit carrier file feeds, COBRA administration handoffs, benefit cost reporting, and enrollment audits. 

Preferred Qualifications

Workday Pro certification in one or more relevant modules.
Experience with third-party HR technology integrations and vendor management.
Exposure to change management methodologies and communication planning.
Prior experience in private equity, financial services, or multi-company real estate environments.
Familiarity with Agile or product management frameworks (backlog management, sprint planning, road mapping tools).

Revantage is a Blackstone portfolio company and a leading provider of corporate services across Blackstone's Real Estate portfolio. Headquartered in Chicago, Revantage supports a diverse and complex ecosystem of portfolio companies (PortCos) spanning residential, commercial, logistics, hospitality, and life-sciences real estate globally — across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific.

Our People Technology team sits at the centre of this multi-entity, multi-jurisdictional operating model. We run a single Workday tenant that serves a federated landscape of PortCos, each with its own workforce, HR policies, compensation structures, payroll requirements, and compliance obligations. About Techdome

At Techdome, we turn AI ambition into enterprise-grade products. Our engineers, designers, and AI specialists build LLM-powered applications, RAG systems, conversational assistants, autonomous agents, and workflow automation for clients in FinTech, Healthcare, E-commerce, EdTech, Logistics, and SaaS. Every product ships with the integrations, security, and compliance that enterprise clients demand.

Why This Role Exists

Anyone can get a GenAI prototype working in a weekend. The hard part is everything after: passing a security review, staying inside budget, keeping costs per query sane, and earning the trust of real users.

We’re looking for a Product Manager who treats that hard part as the real job. You’ll own products end to end, from the first client conversation through launch and long-term growth, and you’ll be the person who spots the vague requirement, the missed handoff, or the quiet risk while it’s still cheap to fix.

What You’ll Own

Product vision and scope

Shape a client’s idea into a clear product definition with realistic milestones, timelines, and budgets.
Go deep on each client’s industry, regulations, and compliance obligations, and convert them into requirements engineers can build from without guessing.

Taking GenAI from prototype to production

Partner with ML engineers to harden LLM, RAG, agent, and automation prototypes into reliable, scalable, and safe systems.
Define the metrics that matter in production, including accuracy, latency, evaluation scores, and cost per query, and review them continuously.
Make sure every AI feature integrates cleanly with client systems via APIs and meets enterprise expectations for security, data privacy, and uptime.

Leading across disciplines

Align UI/UX, frontend, backend, mobile, QA, DevOps, and business analysts so handoffs are explicit and nothing relies on assumption.
Plan team capacity and keep every party accountable to their commitments.
Manage third-party partners, including LLM and cloud providers.

Managing risk, change, and communication

Run structured change control whenever scope, timeline, or budget shifts.
Surface and escalate delivery, technical, and AI-specific risks early: hallucinations, prompt injection, data leakage, bias, and runaway costs.
Track work in JIRA or Azure DevOps and give clients and leadership clear, no-surprise updates.
Use AI tools to accelerate documentation, planning, tracking, and reporting.

What You Bring

Must have

2+ years as a Product Manager shipping complex enterprise software on time and on budget.
Hands-on GenAI experience, ideally having launched at least one LLM, RAG, or agent-based product, plus a solid grasp of the AI lifecycle and its risks.
A track record of leading cross-functional teams across design, engineering, QA, and DevOps.
Working knowledge of Agile (Scrum/Kanban) and Waterfall, and of tools like JIRA, Azure DevOps, Trello, or Asana.
Enough technical depth in the SDLC, APIs, microservices, databases, cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), and CI/CD to challenge estimates and earn engineers’ respect.
Sound judgment on risk, change, vendors, and stakeholders.
Clear, confident written and verbal communication, including with senior client executives.

Nice to have

Familiarity with LLM evaluation, guardrails, and cost-optimization practices.
PMP, PRINCE2, CSM, CSPO, or an AI/cloud certification.
Deep domain expertise in FinTech or Healthcare.
Experience across industries and the curiosity to pick up a new one fast.

How We’ll Measure Success

Day 30: You know how Techdome delivers, you’ve met the team, and you’re up to speed on active client projects.
Day 60: You independently lead at least one project, owning the plan, the risks, and the client relationship.
Day 90: You land a key milestone, make a visible improvement to how we run projects, and have earned the trust of both team and clients.

What’s In It For You

Technically demanding GenAI work across multiple industries.
Daily collaboration with seasoned designers, engineers, QA specialists, and AI experts.
A genuine say in how projects are planned, run, and delivered.
Room to build deep expertise at the frontier of GenAI.

2Base Technologies Pvt. Ltd. is a Kochi-based IT services and software development company established in 2010. We are a full-service technology partner offering technology consulting, custom software development, enterprise application development, web and mobile application development, and digital transformation solutions. We have delivered across Insurance, EdTech, Hospitality, and Travel & Tourism, and we work with clients in global markets including the US and UK.

The Opportunity

We are building our own technology products, with a strong focus on AI-driven solutions, and we are looking for the person who will own what they become. This is a product at the concept and early development stage. You will shape its direction, validate the market opportunity, decide what is built and what is not, and drive it towards commercial success.
As our first dedicated Product Management professional, you will also establish the product function at 2Base: there is no existing roadmap, process or product organisation to inherit.


Key Responsibilities

Define the product vision, strategy, roadmap and long-term direction, and keep the roadmap stable enough to plan against and open enough to change when the evidence changes.
Conduct market research, competitor analysis, and customer discovery to identify and validate product opportunities, and bring the findings into roadmap decisions rather than filing them as reports.
Translate customer problems and business needs into clear product requirements: the outcome and the user problem, specified well enough for Engineering to build against without dictating the solution.
Own feature prioritisation and release decisions with Engineering and UI/UX, and be able to state the cost and the benefit of each choice. A roadmap that only says yes is a backlog.
Identify and evaluate AI, Generative AI and automation opportunities, and assess each on feasibility, scalability, cost and business value before it reaches the roadmap.
Define product success metrics before the work starts, instrument the product to measure them, and read the results honestly afterwards.
Contribute to product positioning, pricing, go-to-market strategy and commercial viability, working with Sales and Marketing.
Build shared context across the organisation so that teams can make decisions without routing every question through you.
Work closely with the Founder, Engineering, UI/UX, Sales and other stakeholders to align on product direction and drive execution.

What You Will Not Own
Product Manager and Project Manager are used interchangeably across the market. At 2Base, they are different roles, so the boundary is stated rather than assumed.
Client project delivery. Project Managers own client engagements, schedules, and escalations.
Engineering architecture and implementation. You own what and why; Engineering owns how. Where the two conflict, you negotiate rather than instruct.
UI/UX design execution. The design function designs. You own the user outcome and brief, review and decide against it.
Final product investment and budget approval. The Founder decides what the product is funded to do and over what horizon. You own the case that decision is taken on.
Client-specific commercial negotiations. Pricing and packaging of the product itself is yours; client contracts are not.

Requirements
Experience

6–12 years in the technology industry, with at least 4 years in Product Management or direct product ownership.
At least one product you took from concept or early development to actual customer usage, with a clear view of what happened after release. A product you inherited fully formed and maintained is a weaker signal than a smaller one you shaped.
A decision not to build something, and what it cost you to hold that line.
Direct work with engineering teams through a build, not across a handover, with enough understanding of software development, technical feasibility, APIs, integrations and cloud applications to judge what a decision will cost.
AI and Emerging Technology
Practical exposure to AI-powered products, Generative AI, machine learning or automation-driven solutions.
The ability to tell a capability apart from a product, and to assess an AI use case on feasibility, scalability, cost and business value rather than on novelty.
Product Judgement

You can describe how you decided what to build: the evidence you had, the evidence you wanted and did not have, and what you did about the gap.
You can reason about a product commercially. Who pays, what for, and what has to be true for the numbers to work.
You can hold a position with a founder, an engineering lead or a client, and change it when the argument against you is the better one. Knowing which situation you are in is the skill.
You write and present clearly. Most of a product manager's influence here travels as writing, and a requirement that is ambiguous on Monday becomes an argument three weeks later.
Ways of Working
You start by asking rather than deciding. The first months are spent understanding users, the business model, what has already been attempted, and how decisions are actually made here.
You work independently and establish your own processes. There is no research function and no analyst to brief.
You influence without formal authority. Nobody in this structure reports to you, and the roadmap holds because people agree with it.
You can make a decision that leaves someone unhappy, explain the reasoning, and keep working with them. Trade-offs are the job, and somebody loses every time one is made.
Education

A Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

What We Are Not Looking For
Stated now rather than at the end of a multi-stage process.
Project or delivery managers looking to change title. The skills overlap less than the market suggests, and this is not a promotion path from delivery.
Business analysts who have written specifications against requirements someone else set. Valuable work; different work.
Candidates whose account of a product is the features it shipped, with no view on whether it should have shipped them.
Anyone who needs an established research function, design system and process in place before they can start.

Benefits
A growth-driven environment with opportunities to lead, innovate, and upskill continuously.

Who is DexCare?

DexCare optimizes time in healthcare, streamlining patient access, reducing waits, and enhancing overall experiences. Guided by our mission – Nobody waits for care – DexCare addresses tech gaps by aligning supply and demand to modernize healthcare infrastructures for an inclusive ecosystem. We are equally committed to our DEIB mission: Creating an inclusive workplace where diversity drives innovation, equity ensures fairness, and belonging strengthens collaboration, enabling everyone to thrive. 


What is DexCare? 

DexCare, a digital care orchestration platform, streamlines care delivery logistics. It empowers healthcare systems to predict constraints and precisely schedule services, optimizecapacity, and cuts operational costs. Currently serving 57 million patients, including Kaiser Permanente and Providence, DexCare ushers in a new era of digital-care access, ensuring health systems can efficiently track and deliver every hour of capacity for consumer ease. 


For more information, visit www.dexcare.com or follow us on LinkedIn. 


About the Role

DexCare is building the AI-first patient navigation platform that health systems rely on to connect patients with the right care, fast. The Platform Foundations team owns the trust and control layer that every product at DexCare — and every customer that integrates with us — depends on: authentication, identity, tenant and license management, and the API gateway that fronts our services.

We're looking for a Technical Product Manager to own this foundation. You'll define how identity and access work across a multi-tenant healthcare platform, balancing security, compliance, and scale with the need for a frictionless experience for end users, administrators, and the engineering teams who build on top of your platform.


What You'll Own

Identity & Authentication: Roadmap and requirements for authentication (SSO, MFA, federated identity), session management, and secure user lifecycle across consumer, provider, and admin personas.

User & Tenant Management: Multi-tenancy architecture decisions, tenant provisioning/configuration, role-based access control, and org-hierarchy modeling that scales as DexCare adds health system customers.

License Management: Product requirements for entitlement models, usage tracking, and license enforcement that support DexCare's commercial packaging and billing needs.

API Gateway: Prioritization for the gateway layer — rate limiting, routing, versioning, and access policies — that other internal teams and external partners build against.

Cross-Functional Partnership: Work closely with Security, Engineering, Compliance, and Commercial teams to ensure the platform meets healthcare-grade security and privacy requirements (HIPAA, SOC 2, FedRAMP) without slowing down product velocity.

Roadmap & Prioritization: Translate platform reliability, security, and scalability needs into a prioritized backlog; make explicit build-vs-buy and sequencing tradeoffs.




What You'll Bring

7-9 years of product management experience, with a meaningful portion of that in platform, infrastructure, or identity/access domains.

Direct experience with authentication/authorization systems, multi-tenant SaaS architecture, or API platform products.

Comfort operating at a technical level — you can read an API spec, participate in architecture discussions, and push back credibly with engineering.

A track record of balancing security/compliance requirements against usability and delivery speed.

Strong written and verbal communication; able to translate technical tradeoffs for both engineering and executive audiences.

Has migrated a legacy system to multi-tenant SaaS with live customers

Experience in healthcare technology, regulated industries, or enterprise B2B SaaS is a strong plus.




Why This Role Matters
Identity and access aren't a back-office concern at DexCare — they're the foundation that makes every other product trustworthy and scalable. As DexCare grows its health system footprint, the decisions you make about tenancy, entitlements, and access control directly shape how fast the company can bring new customers and capabilities online.

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Job Description

Client Services provides a world-class service experience to Visa's clients that begins with pre-sales and continues through onboarding, implementation of new products and services, issue resolution and service optimization.

The Client Services Digital and AI organization is dedicated to simplifying and automating end-to-end business processes across the client lifecycle and making client interactions with Visa straightforward, intuitive, and rewarding through the design, development, and delivery of enhanced digital experiences. As a member of this team, you will play a pivotal role in transforming cross-functional Client Services processes through scalable products, intelligent automation, and AI-enabled solutions.

We are seeking a Senior Product Manager to lead high-impact digital, automation, and AI products that improve Client Services processes across the client lifecycle, including integrations between enterprise platforms and internal and external systems. This role will own product strategy, discovery, solution design, roadmap prioritization, and execution across a portfolio spanning multiple business domains and cross-functional teams, driving measurable client, employee, risk, and operational outcomes in a fast-paced environment.

The ideal candidate is a senior product leader with exceptional execution skills, technical and AI fluency, and a record of solving complex enterprise challenges. They apply rigorous critical thinking, customer empathy, and user-centric design; make sound decisions with incomplete information; influence executive stakeholders; lead large-scale, cross-functional initiatives; and translate ambitious visions into measurable outcomes. This role requires a leader who can operate effectively across business, product, design, technology, and operations teams while maintaining a relentless focus on user experience, business value, and delivery excellence. The successful candidate will help shape the future of our platforms by driving intelligent automation, AI-enabled experiences, and seamless integrations that improve productivity, scalability, and client outcomes, and will provide portfolio-level guidance and mentorship that elevates product management capability across the organization.

Responsibilities

Define and drive the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for a portfolio of digital, automation, AI, agentic, and integration capabilities that improve Client Services processes enterprise-wide across the full client lifecycle and multiple business domains, setting the strategic direction that guides the broader team.

IoT is the only focus area for Silicon Labs and is one of the most visible and fastest growing segments of the semiconductor industry. Our portfolio of industry leading wireless solutions includes Bluetooth, Zigbee, Thread, Z-Wave, Wi-Fi, Wi-Sun, Proprietary Wireless and other emerging technologies driving the next generation of IoT smart connected products. Continuously improves our portfolio offering, balancing business needs with R&D efficiency.
Creates product roadmaps based on various segment inputs to meet the requirements for a diverse range of applications

Define SoC product requirements, features, specifications, and system KPIs for core CPU, co-processors, accelerators, power management, digital and analog peripherals, security sub-system, radio sub-system, and packages.

jobs.sourceTitle: Senior Hardware Product Manager - IoT Wireless
jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
Silicon Labs (NASDAQ: SLAB) is the leading innovator in low-power wireless connectivity, building embedded technology that connects devices and improves lives. Merging cutting-edge technology into the world’s most highly integrated SoCs, Silicon Labs provides device makers the solutions, support, and ecosystems needed to create advanced edge connectivity applications. Headquartered in Austin, Texas, Silicon Labs has operations in over 16 countries and is the trusted partner for innovative solutions in the smart home, industrial IoT, and smart cities markets. Learn more at www.silabs.com.
Meet the Team
IoT is the only focus area for Silicon Labs and is one of the most visible and fastest growing segments of the semiconductor industry. Our portfolio of industry leading wireless solutions includes Bluetooth, Zigbee, Thread, Z-Wave, Wi-Fi, Wi-Sun, Proprietary Wireless and other emerging technologies driving the next generation of IoT smart connected products. With the addition of AI acceleration, rich MCU content combined with best-in-class software stacks, tools and development environments we offer compulsive and complete solutions to customers.

As a member of the Hardware Product Management team, you will be responsible for the Silicon Labs IoT products starting from concept to plan and customer alphas. You will be required to interact with a wide range of cross functional teams including silicon design, product test, validation, software product management & engineering, project management and business management to ensure the best of the products come to the market.

As a team, hardware product management:

Provides leadership and vision on IC product roadmap and requirements.
Continuously improves our portfolio offering, balancing business needs with R&D efficiency.
Creates product roadmaps based on various segment inputs to meet the requirements for a diverse range of applications

This is one of the few functions where you will have the great opportunity to discuss with top executives regarding strategy and execution on a day-to-day basis, thus having invaluable amount of learning. 

Come and join us in our goal to become the undisputed leader in wireless connectivity for IoT! 

Responsibilities
Define SoC product requirements, features, specifications, and system KPIs for core CPU, co-processors, accelerators, power management, digital and analog peripherals, security sub-system, radio sub-system, and packages.
Map market systems application requirements to product use cases, including system block diagrams, compute and peripheral requirements, and protocol stack features and performance requirements for Wi-Fi, Matter, Thread, ZigBee, Bluetooth Low Energy, Bluetooth Classic, Sidewalk, Wi-SUN, and proprietary protocols.
Define hardware and evaluation tools for customers, including debug interfaces such as JTAG, SWD, ETM trace, PTI, virtual communication port requirements, and user interfaces such as push buttons, LCDs, LEDs, analog joysticks, and RHT sensors.
Collaborate with leaders and individual contributors across functional teams such as IC design, product test, software development, product and segment marketing, applications, operations, and sales to develop long-term innovation ideas, roadmap, and silicon definition.
Drive the product development process from concept through definition and pitch the most promising product ideas to executive staff.
Conduct key competitive analysis, including tear-down at the die level and various spec analyses, to provide conclusive takeaways for design, specification, and fighting guides.
Manage the entire portfolio of scalable products with clear mapping to target applications. 

Skills You Will Need
Minimum Qualifications
BSEE/BSCS (or equivalent) and 6+ years of experience in semiconductor product management or IoT industry
Core development experience in IC front end / architecture / verification / embedded systems
Knowledge of key architectural considerations for PPA, including power estimation, die size estimation, and fundamental process node technology principles.
Knowledge of Wireless Modem and RF Design principles for any of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, 802.15.4, and other Low Power Wireless standards
Proven ability to work successfully at a technical level with cross-functional engineering teams, including hardware and software engineers 
Experience developing business cases for Technology investments working with Business Unit partners, sensitivity analysis of business case to variables under consideration. 
Excellent communication and presentation skills, especially to executive management

The following qualifications will be considered a plus:
Development experience in either wireless or wired communication protocols
MBA or equivalent business graduation

Benefits & Perks
Not only will you be joining a highly skilled and tight-knit team where every engineer makes a significant impact on the product; we also strive for good work/life balance and to make our environment welcoming and fun.
· Equity Rewards (RSUs)
· Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

Overview

Join the Intuit Platform and Development Xcceleration group as a Senior Staff Product Manager. The PDX group builds the foundational capabilities that developers across Intuit rely on to build and run flagship applications on cloud native infrastructure at scale. Intuit believes in open source, both as a consumer and a contributor, and our engineers participate actively in communities including CNCF, Istio, and Argo.

We're looking for a product leader who can own two connected platform domains: the systems that provision and run Intuit's cloud infrastructure, and the systems that make Intuit's APIs and services usable by AI agents, not just human developers. You'll set direction for how infrastructure gets provisioned against policy, and for how AI agents discover, integrate with, and operate Intuit's internal services with less and less human intervention over time.

This role carries senior staff scope. You'll set product strategy independently, make tradeoffs other teams will build against, and represent these platforms directly to engineering and executive stakeholders.

Responsibilities

Own the product strategy and roadmap for Intuit's infrastructure orchestration and provisioning platform, working closely with the engineering teams who build and operate it.
Own the product strategy and roadmap for Intuit's agent-readiness platform, which evaluates how usable Intuit's internal APIs and services are for AI agents and drives the work that closes the gaps.
Define the metrics that matter for each platform, from infrastructure reliability and provisioning speed to how much manual work it still takes before an agent can operate a given capability end to end, and use those metrics to prioritize the roadmap.
Partner with the teams that define platform policy, identity, access, lifecycle rules, so that what you build upholds that policy rather than duplicating or drifting from it.
Work with capability teams across Intuit to help them raise their agent-readiness scores, generate the integration assets they're missing, and turn what used to be manual, tribal-knowledge work into something an agent or a new engineer can follow directly.
Represent both platforms to engineering leadership and cross-functional stakeholders, with a clear narrative tying platform investment to developer productivity and to Intuit's broader AI strategy.
Build and run a scrum team based in India, setting the cadence, backlog discipline, and quality bar that let a distributed team ship independently.

Qualifications

10 or more years of product management experience, including platform, infrastructure, or developer-tools products.
Direct experience with AI-enabled products or platforms, with a strong enough technical foundation to work through integration and architecture tradeoffs with engineering.
Strong experience with AI Evals, model evaluations, technical use cases, shared platform capabilities, driving adoption and growth of platform capabilities, and leveraging AI to assess technical capabilities, and agentic PDLC.
A track record of owning a product end to end: setting strategy, defining success metrics, and driving a roadmap that a distributed engineering team executes against.
Comfort partnering across adjacent platform teams where ownership boundaries matter, and judgment about when to defer to another team's policy versus when to push back.
Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical tradeoffs to both engineers and executives.
Experience managing or closely partnering with engineering teams based in India strongly preferred.
Undergraduate degree in computer science or a related technical discipline required. Equivalent professional experience will be considered. Advanced degree or MBA preferred.

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit. Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

Why UKG

At UKG, the work you do matters. The code you ship, the decisions you make, and the care you show a customer all add up to real impact. About The Team & Value Stream

The AI & Platform Value Stream is the engineering backbone of UKG Ready, the teams that determine whether Ready can scale, perform, and evolve at the pace the business demands. We sit within UKG Ready AI & Platform and own the foundational infrastructure, data platforms, AI frameworks, identity systems, and integration capabilities that every domain team in Ready builds on.

The Integration Framework team owns the connective infrastructure that makes UKG Ready an open, composable platform. Every third party system that connects to Ready, every external data feed that flows in or out, every webhook event that fires, every partner integration available in Solutions Exchange, all of it runs on the framework this team builds and operates. That scope includes the Audit Framework (the underlying audit and compliance infrastructure for Ready), encryption services, data import/export pipelines, middleware and integration infrastructure, and advanced webhooks.

The strategic stakes for this team are rising fast. UKG Ready is targeting $1.1B ARR by 2030. One of the six critical engineering prerequisites for that growth is Integration & Partner Scale: a mature inbound/outbound integration framework with monitoring, governance, API metering, and fairness controls that can support reseller growth and ecosystem expansion at volume. The Integration Framework PM owns the roadmap that delivers that capability.

Equally important: Integration Framework is the connective tissue for UKG Ready's AI native future. AI agents connect to external systems through integrations. Agentic workflows that span UKG Ready and third party platforms depend on reliable, fast, observable integration infrastructure. The Workflow and Integration Bryte AI Frontdoor initiative this team owns will define how AI assisted integration creation works in UKG Ready. This PM will shape the platform architecture that enables that.

You will collaborate with PMs across the value stream (Platform Services, Identity & Access, AI Framework, Analytics Platform), with Global Alliances, Solutions Exchange teams, domain PMs across Payroll, HR, and Time & Labor, and with partner engineering organizations.

About The Role

This is a technically demanding, PM role at the intersection of developer platforms, integration engineering, and partner ecosystems. You will own the roadmap for the integration infrastructure that powers every external connection in UKG Ready and the marketplace through which partners reach Ready customers.

You need both depth and range. Deep enough to make credible technical calls on webhook retry semantics, event driven architecture, API versioning strategies, and encryption at the integration layer. Broad enough to translate framework capabilities into partner value, drive Solutions Exchange as a product led growth surface, and build the business case for API monetization. You'll move between architecture discussions with engineers, roadmap reviews with senior leadership, and go to market conversations with the Global Alliances team, sometimes all in the same week.

This role also requires an AI native working style, not as a nice to have, but as a baseline expectation. UKG operates a fully agentic product and development lifecycle: our engineering teams build with AI coding assistants, our PM organization uses AI agents for research, synthesis, and documentation, and the products we ship are themselves AI powered. We're looking for someone who has genuinely internalized this shift, someone who reaches for an AI agent before a spreadsheet, who accelerates their PM work with agentic tools, and who understands how integration infrastructure must evolve to serve agentic consumers, not just human triggered workflows.

You Will

Own the integration framework strategy and evolution. Define the roadmap for the next generation integration framework: V2 enhancements, event driven architecture, advanced webhooks (editable payloads, retry logic, event filtering, webhook marketplace), batch event processing, and a generic transformation engine that reduces integration build time from months to weeks.

Drive Solutions Exchange and partner ecosystem growth. Own the Audit Framework capability. Define the roadmap for the Audit Framework infrastructure underlying compliance and audit logging across UKG Ready. (Platform Services PM owns the Audit Trail Report surface; this PM owns the framework itself: audit event capture, data retention, encryption, and the APIs downstream systems consume.)

Lead data import/export and encryption strategy. Own the Data Import/Export Framework including SFTP, conversion profiles, and bulk data handling, and own encryption services across the integration layer. Define data security strategy at the integration boundary to meet compliance requirements across all active integrations.

Drive the Workflow and Integration Bryte AI Frontdoor. Own the AI powered interface for integration creation and workflow setup, from a partner or admin describing what they want in natural language to a configured, validated integration running in production.

Define integration standards and developer experience. Drive integration standards across domain teams to reduce time to market for new partner integrations through reusable components and configuration driven development. Own the developer portal, API reference materials, and SDK guidance.

Work as an AI native PM and raise the bar for those around you. Use AI agents daily across PRD drafting, technical research, document synthesis, metrics analysis, and stakeholder communications. Model agentic working practices within the team and bring a practitioner's perspective to the platform you are building for.

Communicate strategy and roadmap to senior leadership and partners. Translate integration platform investments into business outcomes for engineering and product leadership. Represent the integration platform story externally to key partner organizations and internally to Global Alliances.

About You

We're looking for a builder. Someone who understands that integration infrastructure is not plumbing, it is product. Someone who has shipped developer facing platforms, has the technical credibility to shape architecture decisions, and has the commercial instincts to drive ecosystem growth and monetization. This role requires both worlds: you need to earn the trust of principal engineers in a webhook architecture discussion and then turn around and build the partner GTM case for the same capability.

jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
Come work at a place where innovation and teamwork come together to support the most exciting missions in the world!

Principal Product Manager, ASPM

Qualys is looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead ASPM (Application Security Posture Management), within the Enterprise TruRisk Management platform. ASPM provides unified visibility, risk-based prioritization, and integrated remediation to help organizations manage application security risk continuously and autonomously. As the PM, you will define the roadmap and execution strategy for how customers discover, consume, prioritize, and remediate application security risk, while driving ideas to increase product adoption and grow the ASPM business.

This is a high-impact role at the intersection of Application Security, vulnerability management, and Agentic AI. You will work closely with Engineering and Design to turn ideas into scalable, customer-facing capabilities; validate them with customers; partner with Marketing on go-to-market execution; and work with Sales to drive adoption and business growth.

What You’ll Own

Define the roadmap, execution plan and success metrics for ASPM. 
Build capabilities that help customers discover, prioritize, and remediate application security risk based on discovery, exploitability, application criticality, and business impact.
Partner with Engineering and Design and Threat teams to build the intelligence foundation for ASPM, including data ingestion, normalization, correlation, enrichment, scoring, and AI-assisted experiences.
Engage AppSec leaders, vulnerability managers, DevOps practitioners to uncover customer problems, validate solutions, and shape the ASPM roadmap.
Shape how ASPM intelligence powers ETM, TruRisk, risk operations, and Agentic AI-driven decision-making.
Partner with GTM teams on launches, enablement, positioning, and competitive differentiation. 


What Success Looks Like

ASPM becomes the application risk intelligence layer for ETM customers.
Customers cut through application security noise and focus on the exposures that matter most.
Qualys research and threat intelligence are transformed into scalable, actionable application security insights.
ASPM drives adoption, expansion, and differentiation for ETM.
AI and automation accelerate analyst productivity and decision-making without introducing black-box risk.


Required Experience

Minimum 8 years of product management experience, including 5+ years in cybersecurity or enterprise SaaS. 
Experienced in one or more of the following domains: ASPM, API security, Web App Security (SAST, DAST, and SCA), Vulnerability Management
Ability to work deeply with engineering, threat research, design, and security teams. 
Strong product judgment, customer discovery skills, and ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear customer value. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills for executive, customer, analyst, and internal audiences. 
Ability to learn quickly and keep up with fast changing AppSec domain
Familiarity with CVE, CVSS, EPSS, CISA KEV, MITRE ATT&CK, and related security frameworks. 


Preferred Experience

Some knowledge of Agentic AI and AI security would be highly preferred
Prior hands-on experience as Application Security Analyst or Pen-tester is a big plus


Why This Role Matters

ASPM is a critical part of Qualys’ vision for Enterprise TruRisk Management. It brings together application findings, vulnerability management, Qualys research, asset context, and business risk to help customers move from reactive application security to proactive, risk-based Application Security Posture Management.

This role will help shape how Application Security, Vulnerability Management, AI, and automation come together to power the next generation of Application Security Posture Management.

Gracenote, a Nielsen company, is dedicated to connecting audiences to the entertainment they love, powering a better media future for all people. We are the content data business unit of Nielsen that powers innovative entertainment experiences for the world's leading media companies. Our entertainment metadata and connected IDs deliver advanced content navigation and discovery to connect consumers to the content they love and discover new ones.

Job Description Great data only matters if it arrives. Gracenote's delivery platform moves millions of pieces of TV entertainment data every day into the backend systems of the world's leading cable, OTT, CE, and digital companies, powering entertainment experiences used by hundreds of millions of consumers.

We are hiring a Director of Product Management to own this platform from our Bengaluru product and engineering center. You will set the product vision and roadmap for our Unified Data Delivery Platform, the centralized repository that consolidates diverse data from across Gracenote into a single Source of Truth, and for the full family of Video metadata delivery solutions that carry that data to clients worldwide. You will lead a team of two product managers in India and partner daily with our engineering teams to deliver against that roadmap.

Delivery is its own discipline. It is where Gracenote's data meets client systems, with all of the schema, integration, scale, and reliability challenges that implies. It is also the tip of the spear. When something goes wrong for a client, delivery hears about it first and is expected to lead the debugging. We are looking for a leader who has lived in this problem space and knows what it takes to run a delivery platform that clients trust.

Responsibilities

Own the product vision and roadmap for the Unified Data Delivery Platform, the new platform being built to deliver all of Gracenote's Video data to clients and partners
Own the portfolio of Video metadata delivery solutions that clients rely on today
Lead, mentor, and develop a team of two product managers in India

Work closely with UX and engineering to deliver the configuration and analytics tools that make the platform successful for clients and internal teams
Serve as the senior product escalation point when delivery issues arise, leading root cause analysis and driving resolution with engineering and client-facing teams
Work with senior management to identify opportunities and risks, including new products, infrastructure strategy, and quality initiatives
Closely manage the cloud infrastructure and costs associated with the data platform

Qualifications

12+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years owning data delivery, distribution, or client integration products
Experience managing and mentoring product managers
Experience building and operating high-scale data or distribution systems
Hands-on experience with XML, JSON, and REST APIs. Actively uses LLMs to write Python scripts and SQL to answer product questions independently
Experience running structured development processes with distributed engineering teams, from requirements through release
Willingness to flex working hours for regular overlap with US and European clients and stakeholders
Excellent verbal and written communication skills

Preferred Skills/Experience

Bachelor's degree or higher. Computer Science or Engineering major is preferable
Experience in OTT, TV broadcast, or supporting customers who develop products for digital content consumption
Development experience with Gracenote, TMS, ROVI, or other structured entertainment databases

Additional Information

Run the program's operating rhythm: steering meetings, status, risk and dependency management, budget and license forecasting, and the decision log.
Maintain the feedback loop from field signal, usage data, surveys, and champion input into roadmap and prioritization changes.
Partner with the Senior AI Enablement Lead, who owns curriculum and delivery, and with AI CoE architects and Platform Engineering on technical dependencies and sequencing.

Required Skills And Experience

Roadmap and Program Ownership

8-10 years in product ownership, program management, or transformation delivery, including 2+ years owning a technology or AI portfolio roadmap at enterprise scale.
Demonstrated ownership of an initiative roadmap from intake through delivery — prioritization under constraint, transparent trade-off decisions, and dependency and risk management across workstreams.
Product-owner discipline: backlog management, clear requirements and acceptance criteria, release sequencing, and saying no with a reason.
Experience building and defending business cases — cost modeling, ROI, and value realization tracking for technology investments.
Vendor and partner management: scoping, SOW support, milestone-based performance management, and clean handoff or exit.

Professional

Change-management instinct — reads organizational resistance accurately and sequences around it.
Experience working in an agile AIDLC (AI-driven software development lifecycle) in a fast-paced environment with high demand and high standards.

Description

Are you passionate about leveraging evolving LLM technology to solve one of Amazon's most fundamental challenges? Do you want to be building the platform that processes over 5 billion customer interactions annually and transforms months of technical work into minutes? As the Principal Product Manager - Technical (PMT) for the Customer Anecdote Miner [CAM] Platform (winner of the 2024 All Amazon Global Door Desk Award), you'll shape the future of how Amazon teams understand and act on customer feedback at unprecedented scale.

We are looking for a Principal PMT who thrives on solving ambiguous, high-impact problems and turning them into clear product strategies that deliver meaningful results at scale. In this role, you will own a multi-year product vision, shape technology investments, and drive cross-organizational alignment to launch products that customers love. You will partner closely with engineering, design, science, and business teams to deconstruct complex challenges into elegant solutions — all while keeping the customer at the centre of every decision. If you are a strategic thinker with deep technical curiosity, a talent for influencing without authority, and a track record of delivering products that matter, we want to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities

Own and drive a multi-year product vision and strategic roadmap, setting direction in ambiguous spaces where the problem, opportunity, and strategy may not yet be defined.
Lead large, complex product initiatives end-to-end with independence — from concept through launch, scale, and iteration — making high-judgment trade-off decisions with long-term platform and business implications.
Partner as a technical peer with engineering, applied science, and design teams to evaluate architecture proposals, identify trade-offs others may miss, and ensure solutions are extensible, scalable, and aligned with strategic goals.
Drive alignment across multiple organizations by influencing senior stakeholders, resolving prioritization conflicts, and building strategic partnerships that shape investment decisions and shared objectives.
Design experimentation frameworks and define success metrics that distinguish between output and outcome measures, using data, customer research, and emerging technologies including generative AI to accelerate learning and validate product hypotheses.

A day in the life

You'll operate at the intersection of evolving ML technology and real-world business impact. A typical day might include:

Working closely with Amazon teams to understand their feedback analysis needs, and onboarding them as users of CAM
Defining platform features and requirements for upcoming releases
Collaborating with ML Scientists and Engineers to build and optimize our offerings
Analysing platform metrics to identify performance optimization opportunities
Contributing to technical design reviews for new features
Reviewing customer feedback and usage patterns to guide product evolution

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree
Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
Experience technical product management
Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
Experience with end to end product delivery
Experience working directly with Engineers on product enhancements

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with and influencing senior level stakeholders
Experience leading engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product

The Product Owner is the execution arm of the product team and is accountable for translating product direction, roadmap initiatives, and customer needs into clearly defined, prioritised, and deliverable work for Agile development teams. Core responsibilities:

Own, maintain, groom, and prioritise the product backlog, ensuring alignment with product goals, customer needs, business value, and delivery dependencies.
Lead backlog refinement and ensure items are clearly defined, appropriately sized, prioritised, and ready for development.
Assess feature requests, enhancements, defects, and competing demands; recommend sequencing and trade-offs in collaboration with the Product Manager.

Requirements and User Stories
Translate roadmap initiatives and customer or business needs into epics, user stories, workflows, business rules, and clear acceptance criteria.
Break down complex initiatives into manageable increments that can be delivered and validated through Agile sprints.
Clarify functional behaviour, use cases, edge cases, and dependencies for Engineering and QA.
Review completed work against acceptance criteria and confirm whether the agreed requirements have been met.

Agile Delivery and Team Enablement
Work as the product domain expert and primary point of contact for the development team on backlog scope and requirement clarification.
Participate actively in sprint planning, reviews, retrospectives, and other relevant Agile ceremonies; support the team in maintaining sprint-level momentum.
Monitor sprint goals, backlog readiness, scope changes, and cross-team dependencies, escalating risks through the appropriate channels.
Partner with Engineering and QA to support feature validation, quality, and delivery against agreed priorities.

Customer and Stakeholder Collaboration
Work with Product Managers and relevant customer-facing teams to understand customer feedback and translate it into actionable product backlog items.
Drive early feedback on new features and incorporate validated insights into backlog refinement and prioritization.
Communicate priorities, scope decisions, requirement changes, and delivery expectations clearly to cross-functional stakeholders.
Build alignment where stakeholders have competing needs, using product priorities and customer value to guide recommendations.

Continuous Improvement and Senior-Level Contribution
Identify opportunities to improve story quality, backlog health, team collaboration, and product delivery practices.
Use delivery and quality feedback to identify recurring requirement gaps, reduce avoidable rework, and improve sprint readiness.
Share product domain knowledge and provide guidance or mentorship to less experienced Product Owners and team members, where applicable.

Role Focus and Responsibility Boundaries
Maintain focus on product backlog ownership, requirement clarity, and sprint-level product execution in alignment with the Product Manager/CPO.
Tier 2 support and technical triage are owned by Support/DevOps teams; project management and Scrum Master responsibilities by Delivery roles; customer demos and training by Enablement/Presales; and code contribution by Development teams.
Other duties as assigned.

8+ years of experience in Product Ownership, product delivery, software product development, or a closely related role, with substantial hands-on Product Owner experience.

Demonstrated experience owning and prioritizing product backlogs for software products, ideally within a global SaaS or enterprise software environment.
Strong capability in writing epics and detailed user stories, defining measurable acceptance criteria, and translating customer needs and roadmap initiatives into development-ready work.
Proven experience working with Agile/Scrum development teams and contributing effectively to sprint planning, backlog refinement, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.
Ability to prioritize competing requirements by considering customer impact, business value, product priorities, effort, and dependencies.
Experience working closely with Product Managers, developers, QA, Support, Implementation, and other cross-functional stakeholders.
Strong understanding of software development lifecycle, Agile delivery practices, and product quality/acceptance processes.
Ability to act as a domain expert for delivery teams, resolve requirement ambiguity, facilitate decisions, and communicate scope and priority changes effectively.
Experience with JIRA and familiarity with Confluence, Agile boards, backlog tools, and customer feedback tools.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, facilitation, organization, and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced, globally distributed SaaS business.
Experience mentoring colleagues or improving product ownership practices is an advantage.
Business-level English proficiency (written and verbal) required.

This is a hard but interesting product and design problem. You're working with regulated financial products, real money, and a spectrum of users that runs from a first-time investor buying their first stock to an active trader running F&O strategies. The job is to make something genuinely powerful feel calm and trustworthy — not to bolt more features onto a busy screen.

You will work with other pod members and a diverse set of stakeholders towards a collective set of objectives. We work on complex technology, scale while iterating quickly and have a bias for impact in everything we do. You will be responsible for evangelizing and aligning all the cross-functional stakeholders on the strategy and plans and work on the execution and delivery to realize the identified opportunity and impact.

Today that means you, the craft, and a close partnership with Business, Engineering and regulated ecosystem.This is a hands-on leadership role, not a manage-from-a-distance one. As the product grows, you'll build and lead the team around it.

Identify and deliver multiple Annual Operating Plan-shaping bets; consistently make correct profitability vs growth calls across portfolio, shift business trajectory with durable levers (pricing, distribution, unit economics, cost-to-serve)

Domain focus: Security products for Network & Zero Trust and MDR & Detection Engineering.

Job Purpose:

Own security product management for Network, Zero Trust and MDR: the product lifecycle, roadmap, adoption and outcomes for the tooling in these domains. You define requirements with the architecture domains, manage vendor delivery, and own the investment case and total cost position.

About the team:

Design Assurance and Product Management makes sure security is designed in before anything is built, and that GSK's security capabilities are run as products rather than projects. Design Assurance independently verifies that solutions meet the architecture standards set elsewhere in Cyber Architecture and Solutions; it writes none of those standards, and that separation is what makes the review worth anything. Product Management owns the security portfolio, vendor governance and investment analytics, and is how GSK manages its managed service vendor as a whole. Platform support engineering moves into this function, with a small internal team retaining oversight while the vendor operates more than 30 platforms and the data fabric under an OTO model. Seventeen roles.

What makes this role different. Zero Trust at GSK is being built from the ground up, so you are not optimising a mature product set — you are sequencing a migration off an estate people are comfortable with, against application owners who will tell you their system cannot tolerate segmentation. You own the product, the roadmap and the investment; Network and Zero Trust Architecture owns the design standards and you do not. You are measured on enforcement coverage and detection quality in production, not on whether tooling was delivered.

Key responsibilities:

This role will provide you the opportunity to lead key activities to progress your career. These responsibilities include some of the following:

Own the product lifecycle and roadmap for Network, Zero Trust and MDR security tooling.
Define product requirements with the architecture domains and track them through build to release.
Own adoption as an enforcement figure — the share of application access brokered through Zscaler or Prisma Access rather than legacy VPN, and the share of the estate under Illumio microsegmentation policy — and act when migration stalls behind an application owner's objection.
Manage Zscaler, Netskope, Illumio and the MDR provider against delivery and detection-quality commitments, including mean time to deploy new detection content and false-positive rates on tuned rules.
Own the investment case and total cost of ownership position.
Run the product governance forum and keep decisions traceable.
Assess new network, ZT and detection tooling on commercial and lifecycle grounds — licence model, data egress cost, operability by the managed service — while Network and Zero Trust Architecture assesses technical fit.
Land the consolidation of overlapping remote-access and proxy estates — legacy VPN concentrators, standalone secure web gateways and point CASB tools — into the SASE platform, on a dated retirement schedule.
Act as the escalation point for the SOC and the network engineering teams when a detection gap or an enforcement-point outage is attributed to the product rather than the service.
Drive the roadmap from identity-based intrusion and lateral movement: adversaries authenticating with valid credentials and moving east-west inside flat segments, which is why segmentation coverage and brokered-access share are the metrics this portfolio is judged on, not licences deployed.
Lead your team in using approved AI tools to improve productivity and ways of working, role-modelling responsible use and follow GSK's Responsible AI, privacy and security requirements.
Apply GxP, GDPR and data integrity requirements to the tooling in scope, so a routine product change cannot disturb a validated system or the records it holds.
Coach domain analysts and peers in product management practice.

Basic Qualifications:

15+ years in cyber security in a regulated environment — domain focus: security products for Network & Zero Trust and MDR & Detection Engineering
End-to-end product ownership of Network & Zero Trust and MDR & Detection Engineering tools — translating threat intelligence and CISO requirements into funded use cases, with 1-3 year roadmaps for investment, consolidation and retirement and published adoption metrics
Vendor evaluation, selection and lifecycle management — value tracked against threat and risk coverage with automated performance reporting, driving decommission where value is not evidenced
Working in parallel with the Security Solution Engineering squad for Network & Zero Trust and MDR & Detection Engineering — aligning use cases and roadmaps to build, test and vendor handover plans, and coordinating with architecture and Design Assurance without owning standards
Evaluating AI-enabled network and detection products — AI-driven detection, GenAI SOC copilots and agentic SOAR — and their vendor AI claims

Preferred Qualifications:

Technical familiarity with Zero Trust enforcement points, segmentation, SASE and SD-WAN, secure remote access, SIEM, SOAR, EDR/XDR and MDR tooling
Product management discipline — roadmaps, adoption and coverage metrics, and decommission business cases
Vendor governance rhythm — QBRs, executive business reviews, SLA management and commercial negotiation input to Procurement
Portfolio analytics, licence utilisation and renewal calendar management, with tracking and alerts automated through dashboards
Product management certification (Pragmatic Institute, SAFe POPM or equivalent) or CISSP

About The Subscription Product And This Role

Sleek's revenue is overwhelmingly recurring: corporate secretary, accounting and compliance services are sold as annual subscriptions, and each year roughly a quarter of that entitlement base comes up for renewal through a process that remains, in large part, manual. Sales and account teams chase, remind, negotiate and collect; the product nudges but does not yet decide. The gap between the renewal rate we achieve and the rate the service quality warrants is revenue leakage, and closing it is the mandate of this role.

Mission: Own the subscription renewal journey from first renewal notice to collected payment, and convert it from a team-driven effort into a system-driven engine that raises the renewal rate and the share of renewals collected automatically.

We are looking for a commercially astute Product Manager on a contract basis who will sit between product, sales and finance and be measured on the renewal number itself. This person is hands on with data and experimentation, comfortable reading a collections ledger and a funnel dashboard in the same sitting, and expects to be in the room when sales sets its weekly renewal targets. The role is a lean one with real ownership over the renewal experience, the auto-renewal and auto-collection mechanics, and the commercial levers that govern them.

Primary Accountability

You own the renewal number and the three levers that move it.

#1: Renewal target, jointly with sales. Own the renewal rate across markets and plans alongside the sales and account management leads. Build the renewal pipeline view that shows every entitlement coming due by cohort, risk and value; agree weekly targets with sales; and own the product-side actions that lift conversion on the cohorts sales cannot reach by hand
#2: Automated renewal and collection. Own the auto-renewal engine and the share of renewals that are charged and collected without human intervention, including payment-method coverage, card and mandate capture at the right lifecycle moments, retry and dunning logic, and the policy for late payment, service restriction and reactivation
#3: Renewal experience and commercial levers. Own the customer-facing renewal journey (notices, reminders, pricing presentation, plan changes, upgrades triggered by usage or compliance complexity) and the experiment programme that tests which messages, timings, incentives and defaults change behaviour, with a bias toward auto-charge by default and clear consent. 

Key outcomes

Renewal rate up, measurably and by cohort: The renewal rate rises against an agreed baseline, with the improvement attributable to specific product changes and experiments rather than to sales effort alone
A larger share of renewals collected automatically: Auto-collection as a share of total entitlements increases through higher payment-method coverage, earlier mandate capture and more reliable retry logic, reducing the volume sales must chase by hand
A single renewal pipeline both sales and product work from: Every entitlement coming due is visible by market, plan, risk and value; sales works the list, product works the levers, and both report to the same number
An experimentation cadence that compounds: A standing programme of tests on renewal messaging, timing, incentives, defaults and pricing presentation, each with a hypothesis, a sample, a read-out and a decision, run on a weekly or fortnightly rhythm
Fewer leaks at the edges: Failed payments, lapsed services, downgrades and silent churn are classified, counted and owned, and the handling of each is either automated or assigned to a named process

What You Will Do

Run a weekly renewal review with sales and account management: what is due, what is at risk, what converted, what failed, and which product change would have changed the result
Pull and model the renewal data yourself: cohort renewal curves, payment-method coverage, failed-payment recovery, time from notice to payment, and the revenue at stake in each segment
Design, launch and read out experiments on the renewal journey, from reminder cadence and channel to pricing presentation, incentives and default settings, and turn winning variants into the standing flow
Specify changes to the auto-renewal engine with engineering: charge timing, retry schedules, dunning sequences, mandate and card capture, plan-change handling and the rules for service restriction and reactivation
Work with finance on collection policy, invoicing, credit terms and the reconciliation of collected renewals, so that what the product charges and what finance recognises agree
Instrument the renewal funnel end to end and publish a dashboard that sales, finance and product leadership read every week
Listen to renewal calls and read customer replies to understand why customers hesitate, and feed those reasons into both the product backlog and sales playbooks
Identify upgrade and cross-sell triggers at renewal (usage, compliance complexity, headcount) and build the prompts and offers that surface them
Ship fast and check your own work: write the spec, review the build, test the flow on a real account, and watch the first week of data

Requirements

4 to 6 years of experience building digital products, with a meaningful portion spent owning a subscription, billing, renewal, retention or monetisation surface where you were measured on a revenue or retention number
Commercially astute: you understand entitlements, pricing, discounting, collections and the P&L consequences of each, and you can hold your own in a conversation with a sales lead and a finance controller
Strong with data and experimentation: fluent in SQL or an equivalent, able to size a cohort, design an A/B test with adequate power, and read the result without an analyst in the loop
Attention to detail: you notice the mis-timed reminder, the failed retry, the wrong currency on the invoice, and you fix it before the customer does
Incredibly hands on: you write the spec, QA the build, pull the numbers and run the review yourself; this is a lean setup with no layer between you and the work
Track record of shipping and iterating on real products used by paying customers, in close partnership with engineering and commercial teams
Must hold existing legal working rights in your country

Youll shape a consistent approach that gives customers a trustworthy picture they can query, report on, and use with agents, rather than another set of disconnected data sources.
