jobs.sourceTitle: Senior Product Manager — Computer Data and Analytics Platform
jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
About DevRev

At DevRev, we're building the future of work with Computer – your AI teammate. Unlike traditional tools, Computer unifies all your data sources, tools, and workflows into a single AI-ready platform, giving employees real-time insights, proactive suggestions, and powerful agentic actions. It extends your existing software with AI-native apps and agents that work alongside your teams and customers – updating workflows, coordinating across teams, and eliminating repetitive work. We call this Team Intelligence: human-AI collaboration that breaks down silos, brings people back together, and frees you to solve bigger problems. Backed by Khosla Ventures and Mayfield with $150M+ raised, DevRev is trusted by global companies across industries.

About The Role

DevRev is hiring a Senior Product Manager for the Computer Data and Analytics Platform – a hands-on product leader who will own the trusted data foundation that makes Computer precise, useful, and safe across every experience.

Computer should not merely report on work. It should understand customer, product, and operational context; reason across it; and help people and agents take the right action. The Computer Data and Analytics Platform makes that possible through a unified, governed, low-latency data layer that turns data from DevRev and connected systems into durable context for humans, applications, analytics experiences, and AI agents.

You will define how data is captured, modeled, governed, queried, and activated across DevRev. The platform will support operational reporting and embedded analytics, while also enabling grounded, context-rich agentic conversations in Computer – helping users ask questions, investigate work, receive trusted answers, and take safe actions in the flow of work.

This is a unique opportunity to build the foundation for an AI-native operating system – where customer context, product telemetry, structured records, events, and machine reasoning converge.

What You'll Do

Lead the Computer Data and Analytics Platform vision and roadmap - Define and scale the platform that transforms operational and product data into reliable, reusable context for analytics, dashboards, applications, APIs, workflows, and Computer. Set a clear strategy for data modeling, query experiences, data freshness, governance, and activation.
Build trusted, AI agent-ready data foundations - Own the product direction for a platform that preserves source-of-record fidelity while making data easy to discover, understand, and use. Shape the abstractions that let Computer and people work with data confidently – including lineage, permissions, access controls, quality signals, and semantic definitions.
Define the data lifecycle from capture to activation - Guide the end-to-end path from source systems and event capture through change data capture, durable query representations, and governed serving layers. Ensure the platform supports real-time and historical workloads without forcing every experience to depend on a single data store or query engine.
Enable precise answers and safe actions with Computer - Partner with the AI platform to make natural-language data experiences dependable. Drive capabilities that allow Computer to retrieve grounded context, generate useful analysis and visualizations, and execute approved actions through clear permissions, guardrails, and auditability.
Build high-performance, flexible query experiences - Shape the experience for interactive analysis, embedded analytics, and developer workflows. Leverage in-process and local query technologies, including DuckDB where appropriate, to deliver responsive, secure experiences for applications, notebooks, and agents.
Design for multiple personas and levels of abstraction - Serve developers, data and product teams, support leaders, GTM teams, and operators. Provide opinionated defaults and ready-to-use experiences for common workflows, while preserving composability for technical users building applications, integrations, and custom data products.
Champion a platform-grade developer experience - Treat data as a core developer product. Prioritize intuitive APIs and SDKs, documentation, modular primitives, observability, extensibility, and a clear path from prototype to production.
Drive platform-wide interoperability - Ensure the Computer Data and Analytics Platform works seamlessly with DevRev’s product data, customer records, connected systems, applications, workflows, and AI agents. Establish the shared data contracts and platform capabilities that power a complete customer and product understanding.

What You'll Bring

8+ years of product management or complementary experience building data platforms, developer platforms, analytics products, AI products, or infrastructure products.
Experience defining products that span data ingestion, data modeling, data quality, governance, querying, and downstream activation.
Strong understanding of modern data architectures, including source systems, event streams, change data capture, lakehouse-style storage, query engines, and serving layers.
Familiarity with embedded and in-process analytics, such as DuckDB, and the trade-offs between local, operational, and centralized query patterns.
Practical understanding of AI-native data experiences, including grounded retrieval, natural-language querying, Text-to-SQL, evaluation, permissions, and safe action execution.
Ability to design products that serve both technical and non-technical users without compromising trust, usability, or extensibility.
A record of partnering deeply with engineering, design, AI/ML, security, and go-to-market teams to ship reliable, scalable platform products.
Strong product judgment in ambiguous, technical environments – with the ability to turn an architectural direction into clear customer value, milestones, and adoption measures.

Why This Role

You will define the data foundation that makes Computer increasingly capable over time. Your work will enable a future where every interaction can benefit from complete, trusted context: Computer can answer with evidence, surface insights at the right moment, automate approved workflows, and help teams build faster on a shared data platform.

This is not a traditional BI role. It is a chance to build the connective layer between DevRev’s product, customer, and operational data – and the intelligent experiences that turn that data into outcomes.

How do we work? 

Whatever your role, our values describe what we ask of each other.

Be a bridger

Look beyond your own role. Ask questions, share context and help others get unstuck. That may mean bringing the right people together or picking up a problem that doesn’t necessarily fit neatly into your job description.

Care loudly

We want your perspective, not just your agreement. Speak up when something isn’t working or someone needs support. Give honest feedback with respect for the person receiving it. Don’t let an uncomfortable conversation become an unspoken problem.

Own the outcome

Take responsibility for the result, not just your part in the process. Use AI to move the work forward, not to outsource your judgment. Make the call, check whether it worked and change course when it didn’t. If something goes wrong, own it and help fix it.

That’s DevRev!

DevRev is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, or any other basis protected by law.

Come join the QuickBooks Desktop team (part of Mid-Market Segment) as a Senior Staff Product Manager, AI Migration & Onboarding Agent.

QuickBooks is Intuit's flagship accounting software, powering millions of small and mid-sized businesses globally. The Mid-Market team is driving a critical transformation: migrating customers from Desktop to cloud-native platforms.

Today, migration from desktop to cloud is high-friction and high-touch. It slows conversion and strains support capacity. Your mission is to change that by building an AI Agent that guides customers through the entire migration journey, from readiness assessment to data migration, configuration, and first productive use.

This is a zero-to-one role. You will own the vision, strategy, and execution for this agent, working at the intersection of LLMs, agentic architectures, and accounting domain knowledge to turn migration from a barrier into a growth engine.

Position Overview

We are looking for a Staff Product Manager, Compute Platform who is passionate about running managed compute services at scale, namely App Platform, Serverless Functions, and Container Registry, and who understands that a great platform experience is built on well-run infrastructure underneath it.

As a Staff Product Manager, Compute Platform at DigitalOcean, you will join a dynamic team dedicated to revolutionizing cloud computing. You will own the product strategy and roadmap for App Platform, Serverless Functions, and Container Registry (DOCR), the managed compute services that turn DO's Droplet fleet into a place where developers can ship without thinking about servers. That means owning both sides of each service, the developer-facing product and the platform economics beneath it, such as how workloads are packed onto compute, what each app, function, or image pull costs to serve, and how processor, virtualization, and container runtime trends shape our roadmap. You will report to the Director of Product and partner day to day with the Hyderabad-based Compute Cloud Services engineering team that builds the business logic, APIs, and control plane for DO Compute, as well as with our Droplet/VPC, Kubernetes, and infrastructure product peers, finance, and GTM. The ideal person becomes the PM who can hold a customer conversation about deploy workflows in the morning and a capacity and margin conversation in the afternoon, the partner engineering trusts on architecture tradeoffs, and a core part of building out the compute platform PM group in India.

What you'll do

Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for App Platform, Serverless Functions, and DOCR, aligned with DO's overall compute platform strategy, and translate them into prioritized, well-scoped features that are simple to use and efficient to run. 
Own the platform economics of these services. Define how apps, functions, and registry storage map onto Droplets and shared compute, track cost to serve per unit of customer workload, and drive utilization, density, and bin-packing improvements with engineering and finance. 
Stay ahead of the compute landscape that underpins the platform, including processor roadmaps from Intel, AMD, and ARM, virtualization and microVM technologies, and container runtimes and isolation models, and translate those trends into platform decisions such as instance sizing, runtime choices, and price/performance tiers. 
Define the end-to-end developer journey across these services, from source repo or container image to a deployed, autoscaled, observable app or function, and remove the seams (auth, networking, registry, logs, billing) that make customers stitch it together themselves today. 
Work backwards from customers. Run discovery with developers, startups, and SMB platform teams, mine support and community signal, and turn it into clear jobs-to-be-done, user stories, and acceptance criteria. 
Own packaging and pricing for platform services, including how compute, egress, build minutes, storage, invocations, and image pulls are metered, how pricing tracks cost to serve, and how the services attach to Droplets, GPUs, managed databases, DOKS, and Spaces. 
Partner with engineering on architecture tradeoffs in the control plane and data plane, such as build pipelines, autoscaling and scheduling behavior, cold start and concurrency for Serverless Functions, registry performance and garbage collection, and multi-region placement. 
Drive performance, reliability, and efficiency outcomes with clear SLOs and cost targets, and champion the fixes that move them. 
Monitor the competitive landscape for managed compute and PaaS offerings, and identify where DO can differentiate on simplicity, price/performance, or both. 
Lead launches end to end with product marketing, docs, sales, and support, and own the results after GA, including adoption, activation, retention, and margin. 

Key metrics

Platform services revenue and attach rate (share of Droplet, GPU, database, and DOKS customers also running App Platform or Serverless Functions, and share pulling from DOCR). 
Infrastructure efficiency, measured as fleet utilization and density for the compute serving these services, and cost per unit of customer workload (per app instance, per invocation, per GB stored and pulled). 
Gross margin per service, and the gap between pricing and cost to serve as the fleet and processor mix evolve. 
Activation, retention, and expansion, measured as time to first deploy and as apps, functions, and registries active at 30/90/180 days. 
Reliability and performance against SLO, e.g. deploy and build success rate, control plane availability, Serverless Functions cold start p95, image pull latency. 

What you'll add to DigitalOcean

8+ years of product management experience, with a proven track record defining and launching managed cloud compute, PaaS, serverless, or container products, ideally where you owned both the customer experience and the unit economics. 
Strong working knowledge of PaaS, serverless, and container registry models, including buildpack-based deploys, function runtimes and triggers, concurrency and cold start tradeoffs, and OCI image build, storage, and distribution. 
Compute fluency. A solid understanding of the cloud compute landscape, including CPU architectures (Intel, AMD, ARM) and their price/performance characteristics, virtualization and microVMs, container runtimes and isolation, and how these choices affect density, latency, and cost. You will not own the hardware roadmap, but you will make decisions that depend on it. 
Cost and capacity acumen, including understanding of compute, memory, storage, and network cost drivers, the ability to build a cost-to-serve model for a multi-tenant service, and experience turning that model into pricing and utilization targets. 
A strong developer-experience instinct and the ability to specify APIs, CLIs, and console flows that feel simple, with a bias toward defaults that work and escape hatches that do not fight the user. 
Data-driven decision making, with the ability to define the right metrics, read utilization and margin dashboards alongside product dashboards, and change course when the numbers say so. 
Excellent communication and cross-functional leadership, with a record of aligning engineering, infrastructure, finance, and GTM stakeholders across time zones. 

Preferred

Hands-on Kubernetes experience (cluster operations, workload scheduling, the operator and Helm ecosystem, or building a platform on top of it). You will not own DOKS, but many of our customers' workloads are Kubernetes-shaped, and that background makes for better tradeoffs. 
Prior experience on an IaaS or compute team, such as VM or bare metal product, capacity planning, or fleet efficiency, before or alongside platform work. 
Experience shipping on or competing with Heroku, Render, Fly.io, Cloud Run, Lambda, Fargate, ECR/GCR/ACR, or similar. 
Familiarity with datacenter fundamentals (rack layouts, power and cooling, network design) at the level needed to have a credible conversation with infrastructure teams. 
Prior experience as an early or lead PM for a product area in a new geography. 
Familiarity with DigitalOcean's existing product portfolio.

Strength in Trust

OneTrust’s mission is to enable innovation through the responsible use of data and AI. We believe that ensuring data is trusted shouldn’t slow teams down—it should accelerate what’s possible. This led us to develop the first technology platform for responsible data use in 2016. Today, with AI representing the latest and most impactful expansion of data yet, OneTrust is once again redefining what responsible innovation looks like. OneTrust, the AI‑Ready Governance Platform™, unifies regulatory intelligence, automation, and connected governance workflows so businesses can continue to move at the speed of AI while ensuring good governance to prevent data misuse at scale. Trusted by thousands of organizations worldwide, OneTrust is shaping the future where trusted data becomes a transformative force for business and society.

Principal PM AI Governance - Runtime Governance

About OneTrust

OneTrust helps organizations operationalize trust through privacy, security, data governance, and responsible technology adoption. As AI governance becomes a board-level and regulatory priority, customers increasingly need structured ways to understand AI systems, assess risk, monitor behavior, and demonstrate compliance over time.

The Challenge

We are looking for a Principal PM to help shape the future of our AI Governance product with a specific focus on observability and enforcement across AI systems. This role is for a product manager who can connect strategy, execution, and technical depth to help us build the right platform capabilities for the next generation of governed AI.

You will help run squad activities and drive clarity across product, engineering, design, and go-to-market stakeholders to ensure we are building capabilities that are durable, differentiated, and ready for where AI governance is heading next. The ideal candidate brings a strong product mindset along with a background in cybersecurity, SIEM and AI/MLOps.

Your Mission

Own and drive product direction for core AI Governance capabilities related to observability, policy enforcement, controls, and signal-driven governance across AI systems.

You Will Help Define How Customers Can

Gain visibility into AI systems, models, agents, and their behaviors over time using SIEM solutions 
Collect and operationalize governance signals across development, deployment, and runtime environments 
Enforce policies to build responsible AI and secure-AI use cases 
Investigate risk, drift, policy violations, and operational issues with confidence 
Connect governance requirements to measurable controls, workflows, and evidence for compliance outcomes 

What You’ll Do

Partner with engineering and design to run an effective squad cadence, maintain clarity on priorities, and turn ambiguous opportunities into actionable product direction 
Define product requirements and roadmap themes for AI observability, enforcement, and governance workflows 
Translate cybersecurity, platform, and AI/MLOps concepts into customer-facing product capabilities with special focus on SIEM and SOAR capabilities. 
Identify the right future-facing platform investments to support governance for models, agents, prompts, evaluations, runtime signals, and policy controls 
Work closely with internal and external stakeholders to understand market needs, technical constraints, and regulatory expectations 
Drive decisions on what signals should be captured, how they should be normalized, and how they should power governance actions

Senior Product Manager, Search, Indexing and Query

Couchbase | Product Organisation | Bangalore, India | Reports to VP of AI Product Management

About The Role

Couchbase is building the operational data platform for AI. Search, indexing and query are the core of it — how data is found, filtered, ranked and returned is what determines whether an application, or an agent, can actually use the data underneath. We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to own that surface area across Capella and Couchbase Enterprise: the SQL++ query experience, secondary indexing, full-text search, and vector and hybrid search.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role for someone who wants to do the work at the Senior level — write the PRFAQ, sit with the customer, push the tradeoff, ship the capability, and own the outcome after launch. Reporting to the VP of AI Product Management, you will partner closely with the query, indexing and search engineering teams, with sales and GTM, and with the broader AI organization.

You do not need to have shipped a query engine or a search product before. We are hiring for the underlying capability, not the resume line — see “Who This Role Is Open To” below.

What You Will Own

Search, indexing and query as a product surface: End-to-end ownership of how customers express and satisfy a query on Couchbase — SQL++ query, global secondary indexes, full-text search, and vector and hybrid search. The roadmap in your area, the PRFAQs and PRDs, the launch, the adoption, and the iteration after launch.

Retrieval for AI applications: Make Couchbase the retrieval layer that RAG applications and agents actually use — hybrid search relevance, metadata filtering, recall and freshness, and cost per query. Work with the wider AI portfolio so retrieval composes with the rest of the platform rather than sitting beside it.

Developer experience for query and indexing: How a developer writes a query, gets an index recommendation, debugs a slow plan, and understands what a query costs. Reduce the number of things a developer has to know before their first query is fast.

Performance, cost and benchmark credibility: Own the performance story for your area. Reproducible benchmarks the field can stand behind, a defensible cost and TCO narrative against MongoDB, Elastic, Postgres and pgvector, and dedicated vector stores, and a clear point of view on where Couchbase wins and where it does not.

Working backwards from the customer: Start with the customer and work backwards. Write the PRFAQ before any code is written. Validate with real, named enterprise customers. Make clear tradeoff calls about what to build and what to defer based on what the enterprise ICP universally needs — not features chasing competitors or one-off requests outside the ICP.

Engineering partnership: Work shoulder-to-shoulder with the query, indexing and search engineering teams. Earn their trust by being technically credible, decisive on scope, and clear on the why. Own the PRD as a living document, not a one-time artifact. Hold the bar on quality, scope, and timing through to launch.

Customer and design partner engagement: Run design partner programs for the capabilities you own. Bring real customer voice into roadmap decisions and back to the broader team. Help build a pipeline of named reference customers willing to talk publicly about what they have shipped.

Cross-portfolio collaboration: Coordinate across Core Database, Capella, Analytics, Mobile and Edge, and the AI Specialist team so the capabilities you own compose cleanly with the rest of the platform. Bring a build-vs-partner point of view to your area.

Sales and GTM partnership: Equip sales, sales engineering, PMM, and partner GTM with what they need to win on search, indexing and query — positioning, demos, competitive context, benchmark data, customer proof points. Be the product owner in deals where the technical depth matters.

External voice: Contribute as the product owner in customer briefings, webinars, blog posts, documentation, and enablement content for the capabilities you own. Support analyst engagements and keynote content led by the Principal PM, PMM, and AR.

AI-driven PM practice: Use AI deeply and visibly in your own product management work — research, PRFAQ drafting, customer synthesis, competitive analysis, benchmark analysis, engineering collaboration. Adopt and contribute to the team’s AI-driven PM and AI-DLC (AI-driven development lifecycle) practices in day-to-day execution.

Raising the bar: Share what works. Contribute to PRFAQ and PRD standards, interview loops, and onboarding. Mentor associate and early-career PMs as the team grows.

What You Will Deliver

PRFAQs and PRDs for the capabilities you own, validated with named enterprise customers before engineering starts.

Shipped capabilities across query, indexing and search with measurable adoption and at least one named reference customer per major launch.

A published, reproducible performance and cost position for your area that sales and engineering both stand behind.

Clear, defensible tradeoff decisions visible to engineering, sales, and GTM. The team knows what is in, what is out, and why.

Sales and GTM enablement that the field actually uses — measured by pipeline influence and win-rate signals, not enablement-decks-produced.

Contributions to the broader platform narrative — customer-facing content, blog posts, and documentation in partnership with the AI Specialist team, PMM, and AR.

Visible AI-driven PM practice — concrete examples of AI-DLC in your daily work that the rest of the team can learn from.

Must Have

Seven or more years in product management, with at least three on a technical platform — database, data infrastructure, search, analytics, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, or AI infrastructure.

Systems depth. You can reason about latency, throughput, recall, index structures, query plans, memory and storage tradeoffs, and cost per operation. Given a benchmark or a slow query, you know what to ask next.

Customer obsession and working-backwards rigor: You start with the customer and work backwards. You write PRFAQs before code. You can tell which feature requests reflect universal ICP needs and which are noise, and you make the call clearly.

Engineering credibility: Engineers want to work with you. You hold your own on architecture, are decisive on scope, and own the why behind every tradeoff.

Cross-functional trust: Sales trusts your roadmap. GTM trusts your enablement. Marketing trusts your narrative. You build durable working relationships outside your own team.

AI-driven PM practice: You already use AI in your own PM work — research, PRFAQ drafting, customer synthesis, competitive analysis — and you can point to concrete examples.

HackerRank helps companies like NVIDIA, Amazon, and Microsoft hire and upskill the next generation of developers based on skills, not pedigree. Our platform is trusted by over 2,500 of the world’s most innovative companies to build strong engineering teams ready for what’s next.

Software has entered an era where humans and AI build side by side. As this shift accelerates, the definition of strong technical talent is changing. We give companies better ways to identify and invest in next-generation skills.

People at HackerRank care deeply about the impact of their work and sweat the small details so our customers can be wildly successful with products they genuinely love to use. We move with urgency and believe great outcomes come from high standards.

About The Role

HackerRank Interviews is a live technical interviewing platform designed to evaluate how candidates solve realistic engineering problems, not just whether they can pass an algorithm test. Candidates and interviewers collaborate in a shared workspace using coding tools, production-style repositories, and Plan-Build-Review tasks. The platform also supports observable AI-assisted development, letting teams assess how candidates prompt, review, and apply AI-generated work, with observation tools and post-interview reports giving hiring teams clearer, structured evidence for decisions.

In this role, you'll help lead the Interviews product - an AI-native, pair-programming interview experience that gives interviewers the ability to collaborate with candidates on real-world problems and code repos. You'll shape how the platform evolves across richer ADE experiences (harnesses like Claude Code and Codex CLI), Chakra Assist for evaluation, richer session observation (screen sharing, A/V), and reporting across in-product, exports, APIs and MCP. You'll work closely with engineers as collaborators and as the product's core customer and user base including senior engineering leadership as stakeholders who care deeply about this space.

What You Will Do

Own the roadmap for how HackerRank Interviews evaluates AI-assisted development including richer ADE harnesses, Chakra Assist, and session observation capabilities.
Define how the platform captures and surfaces signals on how candidates prompt, review and apply AI-generated work, so interviewers get clearer, structured evidence.
Drive the reporting and integration strategy across in-product reporting, exports, APIs and MCP.
Engage directly with engineering customers and users including senior engineering leadership as the primary audience for this product, translating their needs into roadmap decisions.
Represent the product in high-visibility, customer-facing moments with composure, including when executives engage directly and unexpectedly.
Partner closely with Engineering and Design to ship production-quality, AI-native interview experiences.
Embrace AI - in how we operate, as well as in the product.

Who You Are

Overall 7+ years of total professional experience including at least 1 year of hands-on Software Engineering.
5+ years of Product Management experience, preferably building B2B SaaS, enterprise products and/or tech services and/or platforms, and you are currently working as a PM today.
Comfortable being the technical/product voice in a room full of engineers, including stakeholders like senior engineering leadership
Able to stay composed and sound under sudden high-visibility pressure for example, a CTO persona dropping into a live customer channel.
A strategic thinker who can evaluate complex challenges, prioritise effectively, and balance short-term progress with long-term success.
Deeply passionate about AI using it as a reflex across your own workflows, not just in the product you build.
Ability to deep dive into ambitious problem statements and create customer value.
Proven track record of successfully launching and growing new products and/or significant features.
Ability to work in a fast paced cross team, cross geo environment and to deliver on a common vision.
Ability to work with engineers, designers and analysts and be comfortable presenting to non-technical/business stakeholders and customers.

Even better if you have

Hands-on fluency with agentic coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Copilot Workspace, or similar) deep enough to reason about what a good AI-assisted engineering actually looks like.
Experience designing or owning a GTM motion where the buyer and user were engineers or engineering leadership, rather than a traditional non-technical economic buyer.
Experience operating in a lean, founder-style team with no dedicated marketing support i.e., you've personally built your own sales decks, messaging and customer-facing materials before, not just briefed a marketing team.
Background in HR tech, talent assessment, or technical hiring.
Experience building reporting/analytics or API-level integrations (e.g. MCP, data exports) for a technical audience.

You will thrive in this role if you

You are a builder at heart. You enjoy creating something from scratch, transforming ideas into tangible, high-impact products.
Ambiguity excites you. You’re comfortable working in undefined spaces, carving out clarity where little exists, and defining a clear vision and strategy.
You take a customer-first approach. You excel at identifying unmet customer needs and turning those insights into innovative product solutions.
You are a strategic thinker. You can evaluate complex challenges, prioritise effectively, and make decisions that balance short-term progress with long-term success.
You thrive in fast-paced environments. You’re energised by working on high-impact initiatives where priorities can shift as you gain new insights.
You have a bias for action. You’re not afraid to experiment, iterate, and learn quickly in pursuit of delivering exceptional outcomes.
You are deeply passionate about AI. You’re in the weeds and trying out AI tools constantly and are at a point where you are using AI as a reflex to try and automate several workflows in your life and 10x yourself.

Role: Product Manager - AI Services

Location: Bangalore (Quarterly visit for 2 weeks)

Function: Product Management

Reports to: Director, Packaging Intelligence

Are you... 

Passionate about architecting large-scale cloud platforms? 
Excited to define technology that powers an entire portfolio of products, not just a single application? 
Interested in building the industry's leading AI-native Product Intelligence Platform? 


If so, we'd love to meet you.

Why Esko? 

Esko, part of Veralto (NYSE: VLTO), is the global leader in packaging and product lifecycle solutions. More than 25,000 customers across 140+ countries rely on Esko to design, manage, manufacture, and deliver products found on store shelves every day. Packaging for 9 out of 10 major consumer brands is managed using Esko solutions. As we enter our next phase of growth, we're making significant investments in cloud, AI, and platform engineering to build the future of product innovation.

Our vision is to create the industry's leading AI-native Product Intelligence Platform. This modern, multi-tenant cloud platform unifies product, packaging, regulatory, quality, manufacturing, and supply chain data into a single intelligent ecosystem. By combining cloud-native architecture, intelligent automation, and AI-powered insights, we're helping global consumer goods, life sciences, and manufacturing companies innovate faster, improve compliance, reduce waste, and bring products to market with greater speed and confidence.

About The Role

As Product Manager for AI Services, you will own the product lifecycle for a shared foundation of AI capabilities that Esko's internal teams build on rather than re-invent - enabling them to solve customer problems that were previously out of reach with optimal speed and efficiency.

Cross-functional collaboration sits at the core of the role. You will coach internal teams, consolidate their needs to find common ground, work with technical and design stakeholders to agree the best approach, and document clear, testable requirements that are reviewed and approved before development begins. The result is a coherent, prioritized backlog and roadmap that reflects the combined needs of Esko's product teams and aligns with company strategy and AI transformation objectives.

You will keep stakeholders updated as work progresses, then support them through acceptance testing, triage and implement change requests, and drive adoption of the services in production. Ongoing success management is central: keeping services aligned with evolving team and customer needs while maintaining a generalized approach and backwards compatibility, and growing capabilities in line with advances in technology and market expectations. You will track adoption and key performance metrics to demonstrate impact and identify where more focus is needed.

As a key member of the Esko AI team, you will also help shape the strategic vision for Esko's AI initiatives through brainstorming, thought leadership, customer discussions and events.

What You Will Do

Own and prioritize the product backlog for AI Services – a shared collection of common AI capabilities leveraged by Esko product and engineering teams.
Proactively gather needs from cross-functional product teams and turn them into clear, well-scoped requirements for the Esko AI engineering teams.
Act as a bridge between Esko AI and other cross-functional teams - product, engineering, and commercial – to ensure their success in building AI-powered capabilities that deliver on the intended customer value.
Help other teams to bootstrap their own AI initiatives on top of the shared capabilities: clarifying what already exists, what needs to be built, and how to get started.
Weigh competing requests from multiple stakeholders against the long-term company strategy and priorities, while documenting risks and expected trade-offs.
Define and maintain adoption / success metrics for the shared capabilities - and use them to continually re-prioritize the backlog and indicate risks and areas of additional focus.
Communicate roadmap, priorities, and trade-offs clearly across engineering, product, and leadership stakeholders.


What We Are Looking For

At least 5 years’ experience in a Software Product Management role, preferably including ownership of a platform, API or other shared-services product used across multiple internal teams.
Undergraduate or master’s degree in computer science or related discipline.
Native or fluent proficiency in English.
Experience initiating, deploying, and scaling AI-powered capabilities in production, with a track record of managing the development cycle from proof-of-concepts or early-stage ideas into production capabilities that other teams depend on.
Experience acting as a liaison in a large, global organization with multiple cross-functional teams - gathering and distilling requirements from varied stakeholders, aligning competing priorities, and driving toward a successful shared outcome.
Strong product management fundamentals: backlog ownership and refinement, roadmap creation & communication, and the ability to write clear, unambiguous requirements for engineering to build and test against.
Comfort operating at the boundary between a platform team and the product teams that consume it, balancing shared needs and central objectives against individual team priorities and timelines.
Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to work fluently with both technical and business stakeholders alike.


Preferred Experience

Experience in packaging graphics or the wider graphic arts industry is strongly preferred. 


What Success Looks Like

Teams across the business ship AI-powered capabilities that solve valuable customer problems by leveraging a shared foundation of AI Services, rather than “re-inventing the wheel”.
Ideas and concepts forged by different teams are assessed for potential development as centralized AI services.
A roadmap for AI Services is maintained and accurately describes the status of current and plans for future objectives.
The Esko AI engineering teams work from a clearly prioritized backlog.
Cross-functional teams know exactly who to talk to when they want to bootstrap an AI initiative; and that person offers guidance on opportunities, prioritization and planning.
AI services are clearly explained and documented, with measures taken to minimize any roadblocks or barriers to successful adoption.
AI Services grows as a coherent whole rather than fragmenting into one-off, team-specific solutions.
A class-leading set of capabilities provide a powerful base for Esko cross-functional teams to transform the value of our software using cutting-edge AI technologies.


At Veralto, we value diversity and the existence of similarities and differences, both visible and not, found in our workforce, workplace and throughout the markets we serve. Our associates, customers and shareholders contribute unique and different perspectives as a result of these diverse attributes.

Unsolicited Assistance

We do not accept unsolicited assistance from any headhunters or recruitment firms for any of our job openings. All resumes or profiles submitted by search firms to any employee at any of the Veralto companies, in any form without a valid, signed search agreement in place for the specific position, approved by Talent Acquisition, will be deemed the sole property of Veralto and its companies. No fee will be paid in the event the candidate is hired by Veralto and its companies because of the unsolicited referral.

About The Role

HighLevel’s Commerce platform is the system of record for how our customers sell — what they offer and how it is priced, how orders get fulfilled, and how money moves: payments in, invoices out, and books that balance . It spans product information, pricing, taxes, and channels; fulfillment and inventory; and the full finance stack of payments, checkout, invoicing, and ledger — together powering commerce for a global base of agencies and businesses operating at scale.

We are seeking a Group Product Manager, Commerce , to lead product across three connected verticals — Business Operations, Fulfillment Operations, and Finance — and the team of Product Managers who own them. You will set the strategy for the end-to-end commerce lifecycle, from catalog to cash , and be accountable for the coherence, reliability, and growth of the platform as a whole.

The ideal candidate is an experienced product leader who has managed and grown other Product Managers , and who can zoom from platform strategy down to the details of a pricing engine, a fulfillment flow, or a ledger entry. You lead through your team, raise the bar on product craft , and turn a broad, interdependent surface area into a clear, sequenced roadmap.

Your mission: To build a coherent, reliable, and extensible commerce platform — spanning what customers sell, how it is fulfilled, and how they get paid — and to build the team that delivers it, so HighLevel’s customers can run their entire business on us.

What You’ll Do

Set Commerce Product Strategy – Own the vision and multi-quarter roadmap across Business Operations, Fulfillment, and Finance , translating a broad, interdependent surface area into clear, sequenced priorities.

Lead & Grow a Team of PMs – Manage, mentor, and hire Product Managers across the verticals, setting a high bar for product craft and owning their performance, development, and career growth .

Own the End-to-End Commerce Lifecycle – Be accountable for the full catalog-to-cash journey — product information and pricing, fulfillment and inventory, payments, invoicing, and ledger — as one connected system.

Drive Platform Coherence – Ensure shared contracts like the analytics engine, layouts, and reporting are designed once and reused, so the verticals compose into a single, consistent platform rather than a set of silos.

Deliver Business Operations – Guide the PIM, pricing, taxes, channel configuration, loyalty, and analytics roadmap that lets merchants define what they sell, to whom, and at what price.

Deliver Fulfillment Operations – Steer fulfillment, inventory, and the upcoming warehousing, time-clocking, and metering charters so what was sold reliably reaches the buyer.

Deliver Finance – Own the payments, checkout, invoicing, and ledger/accounting roadmap, ensuring money moves securely and the books balance across providers and external systems like QuickBooks and Xero.

Own Outcomes & Metrics – Drive measurable growth in GMV, transaction success, merchant adoption, and reliability , using data to prioritize across a large and competing set of bets.

Partner with Senior Stakeholders – Work closely with engineering, design, finance, operations, and leadership to align on strategy, resourcing, and trade-offs, and represent Commerce in company-level planning.

Balance Delivery & Long-Term Bets – Keep near-term charters shipping on time while investing in the platform foundations that compound over the next several years .

Raise the Operating Bar – Establish the rituals, specs, and quality standards — discovery, prioritization, launch, and review — that make the team predictable, fast, and outcome-driven .

Who You Are

Experienced People Leader – You have managed and grown Product Managers, and you get energy from multiplying your impact through a strong, well-run team .

Platform & Commerce Depth – You have led product across commerce, payments, fintech, or a comparable transaction-heavy platform , and understand how catalog, fulfillment, and finance fit together.

Strategic and Execution-Focused – You can define a multi-vertical strategy and still hold your teams to crisp execution , ensuring ideas translate into shipped, measurable impact.

Systems Thinker – You see the interdependencies across modules and design for coherence, reuse, and shared contracts rather than one-off solutions.

Outcome- & Customer-Centric – You balance business goals, risk, and trust, keeping the merchants who run their business on the platform at the center of every decision.

Highly Data-Driven in Ambiguity – You are comfortable prioritizing across a broad, messy portfolio, using data to make sharp trade-offs without waiting for perfect information.

What You’ll Bring

8+ years of Product Management experience , including 2+ years directly managing Product Managers , and 10+ years of total professional experience. 
A track record of leading product across a large, multi-team surface area — ideally in commerce, payments, fintech, or platform/SaaS — with measurable business impact. 
Proven people leadership : hiring, developing, and retaining strong PMs, and building the operating rhythm of a high-performing product team. 
Strong platform and systems judgment , with the ability to reason about how pricing, fulfillment, payments, invoicing, and ledger interconnect . 
Experience partnering with senior engineering, design, and business stakeholders to set strategy, secure resourcing, and drive company-level outcomes.

About the Role
The Staff Product Manager - Data & Analytics supports the definition and evolution of Apteans semantic data models and Analytics Packages across business domains and products. The role translates business processes, metrics, reporting requirements, and underlying product data into reusable semantic definitions that can support analytics and AI use cases. Working closely with domain SMEs, customers, Product, Data Engineering, and Architecture, this role drives requirements from discovery through definition, technical validation, and customer validation. The role requires a strong combination of product thinking, business analysis, analytics, and hands-on understanding of relational data and data modeling.
We need a candidate who sits with an ERP SME or business user, understand the business process; inspect the underlying data/schema; define the business entities/KPIs; map source concepts to the semantic model; write requirements detailed enough for Engineering; validate the implementation (reports, AI query, or Agent outputs) with SMEs/customers.
Knowledge:
Requires strong working knowledge of data and analytics concepts, including relational data models, business entities and relationships, semantic modeling, analytical metrics/KPIs, and data transformation from operational systems into analytics-ready structures.
Requires the ability to understand business processes and reporting requirements and translate them into detailed data and semantic-model definitions. You must be comfortable analyzing source schemas, tables, fields, relationships, and existing reporting assets in partnership with Engineering and domain experts.
Requires working knowledge of product management and business analysis practices, including requirements definition, customer and SME discovery, prioritization, documentation, validation, and cross-functional product development.
Knowledge of enterprise software, ERP systems, modern cloud data platforms, BI tools, and AI-enabled analytics is preferred.
Complexity:
Works across multiple business domains, ERP/product schemas, and analytics use cases where business terminology, source data structures, and customer requirements may differ.
Translates sometimes ambiguous business questions and existing reporting requirements into standardized entities, measures, dimensions, relationships, KPIs, and semantic definitions that can be reused across products and customers.
Balances standard product requirements against ERP-specific and customer-specific requirements and identifies where extensions to the governed model are required.
Works through dependencies across Product, Engineering, Architecture, domain SMEs, Professional Services, customers, and other stakeholders to move semantic-model and Analytics Package work from discovery through validation.
This reflects the actual scope in the resourcing case: reusable semantic models are intended to span Finance, Sales, Procurement, Manufacturing, Inventory, Quality and other domains, with iteration occurring across ERPs and eventually non-Aptean systems.
Supervision:
Works with a high degree of independence within defined product priorities and objectives.
Receives strategic direction from the Director, Product Management - Analytics & Data Products and independently drives assigned semantic-model domains and Analytics Package workstreams.
Coordinates work across technical and business stakeholders but does not initially have direct people-management responsibility.
Escalates significant product, data, architecture, and prioritization decisions where broader alignment is required.

  • Define business semantics and domain models.
  • Lead discovery with product SMEs, customers, and internal stakeholders to understand business processes, entities, relationships, terminology, business questions, metrics, and KPIs. Translate these inputs into detailed, reusable semantic-model requirements and domain definitions.

  • Plan and conduct validation sessions with domain SMEs, customers, and implementation teams to confirm that semantic definitions, KPIs, business rules, and Analytics Packages accurately represent real-world processes and reporting needs. Convert validation findings into prioritized product requirements and model improvements.

  • Compare requirements and source structures across ERP products and customer environments to distinguish reusable business concepts from product- or customer-specific requirements. Help establish canonical definitions while identifying where governed extensions are necessary.

jobs.sourceTitle: Product Manager: Growth and Guest Experience
jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
Product Manager: Growth and Guest Experience

Location: Mumbai, full time, in office

Experience: 3 to 5 years


About the role

You will help us answer a question we care about deeply: how do we use technology to make Hunger Inc. more loved, more connected and more scalable? You will think with the founders about guest relationships, community, loyalty, CRM, customer journeys and AI, and turn the best ideas into products that guests love and teams use.


What You'll Own


1. Create our community and loyalty ecosystem

We're exploring what a connected community and loyalty programme could look like across Hunger Inc. But we don't believe loyalty should begin and end with points and discounts. We believe it starts with recognition, trust, generosity, access and belonging. You'll help design, prototype and launch experiences that bring this philosophy to life. That could mean cross-brand discoveries, personalised gestures, special access, community experiences or rewards that feel genuinely meaningful. Your responsibility will be to translate these ideas into a product roadmap, work with engineering to bring them to life and measure whether they actually strengthen customer relationships.


2. Drive measurable growth through experimentation

You'll identify opportunities across customer acquisition, conversion, retention, repeat purchase frequency and lifetime value. Establish baselines, develop hypotheses, run experiments and measure results. You'll also explore how AI can accelerate product discovery, customer analysis, experimentation and prototyping. We want someone who can connect customer insights to commercial outcomes, not just produce interesting dashboards.


3. Supercharge our AI-led CRM

We already use SuperLeap, an AI-native CRM platform. Your challenge is to unlock more of its potential. Work with our teams and technology partners to connect customer information, understand behaviour, build meaningful segments and develop intelligent customer journeys. Think lifecycle marketing, automated engagement, customer retention, repeat purchases, personalised recommendations and identifying opportunities to grow customer relationships. We don't want a CRM that simply stores customer information. We want one that helps us understand what customers love, why they return and how we can serve them better.


4. Build a connected understanding of our customers

Our customers interact with us through Shopify, restaurant reservations, POS systems, gifting enquiries, customer service, WhatsApp and multiple other channels. Today, much of that information lives in different places. You'll help define the product strategy for a connected customer intelligence platform, working with engineering to establish customer identities, useful profiles and a clearer understanding of behaviour across brands. The ambition is to move beyond transactions and develop a meaningful understanding of our guests, with appropriate consent and privacy protections.


What youll bring

35 years of experience in product management, growth product, consumer technology, e-commerce or a related discipline. A conventional product management background isn't mandatory, but you should have demonstrated ownership of a product or feature that real customers have used.


Required Skills

  • Strong understanding of product discovery, user research, product roadmaps, PRDs, prioritisation and experimentation.
  • Hands-on analytical ability, including SQL, spreadsheets, funnel analysis, cohort analysis, retention metrics and customer segmentation.
  • Experience taking products or features from identifying a problem through launch, adoption and measuring outcomes.
  • Understanding of APIs, customer data architecture and technical integrations sufficient to collaborate effectively with engineers.
  • Familiarity with CRM systems, customer journeys, lifecycle marketing and growth experimentation.
  • Practical experience using AI tools for research, analysis, prototyping or product development.
  • Strong written communication and the ability to translate complex ideas into clear requirements.
  • Comfort working directly with operational teams and customers rather than relying entirely on dashboards.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with Shopify, SuperLeap or comparable CRM/CDP platforms.
  • Familiarity with Mixpanel, Amplitude, GA4, Metabase or similar analytics platforms.
  • Experience building loyalty, membership, community or customer retention products.
  • Understanding of customer identity resolution, data privacy and personalisation.
  • Experience in D2C, consumer brands, hospitality, retail or marketplaces.
  • Ability to build functional prototypes using AI-assisted development tools.
  • Experience working in a founder-led business or small cross-functional product team.

What success looks like

You've helped us build a more connected understanding of our customers, unlocked meaningful capabilities within our CRM, and launched customer experiences that improve engagement, retention or repeat behaviour. You can demonstrate what changed, why it changed and what we learned.


What this role is not

This isn't a traditional marketing role where you manage campaigns and content calendars. It isn't a role where you write PRDs, hand them to engineering and move on. And it isn't about launching a loyalty programme simply because every other brand has one. We want someone who takes responsibility for identifying the right problems, building the right experiences and understanding whether they actually worked. 


We're looking for someone who wants to engineer better customer relationships, not just manage customer databases.

Role Overview
As the Product Manager for Distribution, you are the "Full-Stack" owner of the value stream connecting our suppliers to our customers. You will move beyond tactical ticket-writing to drive the "Why" and "What" for both customer sales and supplier purchasing capabilities. This role is part of our Functional Product Stream, focused on solving pervasive market problems to drive adoption and revenue.
Core Responsibilities
Your work is structured around the Product Management Lifecycle (PMLC), focusing on outcome-based decision gates rather than feature output.
1. Discovery & Strategy (The "Why")
  • Market Sensing: Conduct biweekly customer and supplier interactions to validate that identified problems are urgent and pervasive.
  • Problem Validation: Use data from Win/Loss reports and Customer Advisory Boards (CAB) to build evidence-based business cases.
  • Opportunity Canvasing: Define the market driver, competitive landscape, and economic impact (ROI) for new distribution initiatives.
2. Solution & Design (The "What")
  • Roadmap Ownership: Maintain a 3-year Now/Next/Later roadmap that balances customer sales features, supplier integration, and technical health.
  • Ruthless Prioritization: Apply the RICE framework (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) to the backlog to ensure we focus on "Return on Effort".
  • Constraint Definition: Clearly distinguish between MVP (Technical Prototype) and MLP (Minimum Lovable Product) to prevent scope creep.
3. Delivery & Market Alignment (The "How")
  • Squad Leadership: Act as the strategic lead for a group of Autonomous Squads (Atomic Scrum Units), collaborating with a Tech Lead and Product Designer.
  • GTM Readiness: Partner with Product Marketing to ensure Sales, Support, and Customer Success are operationally ready for new releases.
  • Success Analysis: Post-launch, measure actual adoption and revenue against the original business case metrics to decide whether to Pivot, Persevere, or Kill.
4.Success Metrics (KPIs)
In a product-led organization, you are measured on Outcomes, not outputs:
  • ARR: Supporting growth goals for sales.
  • Customer Retention: Ensuring users get continuous value from the distribution module.
  • Outcome Achievement: Meeting the specific success criteria defined in your Business Cases (e.g., reducing purchasing lead times).
  • Strategic Alignment: Ensuring 100% of your roadmap items are scalable for multiple customers and not bespoke requests. Qualifications
  • Experience: 5-10 years of experience in Product Management within supply chain, ERP, or distribution software is highly preferred.

  • Decision Making: Ability to make "Green Light" investment recommendations based on hard data (logs, usage stats) rather than "gut feel".
  • Tooling: Proficiency in Aha! for strategy/roadmapping and Jira for execution management.

Who are you :

You are a customer-focused, outcome-driven Product Manager who connects customer problems, business priorities, and technology to deliver meaningful, measurable product outcomes. You combine strong discovery, analytical judgment, and commercial and technical fluency to make evidence-based decisions, prioritize opportunities, and balance customer value, business impact, and technical feasibility.
You would own a defined product or workflow, working with Engineering and Design from discovery through adoption and results.
You collaborate closely with Engineering, Product Design, and cross-functional stakeholders, bringing clarity to product decisions and maintaining accountability from discovery through delivery, adoption, and continuous improvement.

2. Product direction and prioritization
Translate product direction into focused priorities and a roadmap connected to outcomes.
Compare options using customer value, business impact, uncertainty, dependencies, risk, and lifecycle cost. Make or recommend continue, change, pause, or stop decisions within your mandate.

3.Delivery, adoption, and measurement

4. Complete solutions and responsible ownership

You will help shape the next generation of television audience measurement as viewing continues to fragment across traditional and streaming platforms. Where will your career take you next? Let’s find out together.

At Zurich Cover-More, we’re proud to be one of the world’s leading travel insurance and assistance providers. Each year, we protect more than 20 million travellers worldwide, making sure we’re there every step of their journey with proactive care, personalised cover and specialist support. Zurich Cover-More partners with many of the world’s best-known brands – think major airlines, travel giants, top banks, credit card providers, and large retailers – to deliver more care, more cover, for all.

Launched in December 2024, Zurich Cover-More is the global travel brand of Zurich Insurance Group, one of the world’s leading multi-line insurers. Our family of customer-facing brands includes trusted names like Travel Guard, Cover-More Travel Insurance, Travelex Insurance, Universal Assistance, World Travel Protection, Freely, and Blue Insurance. Together, we’re redefining what it means to travel safely and with confidence. Whether it’s a long-awaited holiday, a last-minute business trip, or an unexpected detour, we deliver in the moments that matter.

About the opportunity:

When a traveler's bag goes missing or a trip is cancelled, what happens next runs on our operations: claims, policy changes, refunds, documents and service requests. We're moving that work onto one enterprise case management and BPM platform, used by up to 2,000 people across North America and Australia–New Zealand first, then Europe.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own it. You'll decide which processes move first, lead our BPM analysts in the US and India, and work with our implementation partner to deliver workflows that cut handling time and manual effort.

What you’ll be doing:

Own the case management and BPM vision, roadmap and backlog across claims, servicing and operations
Rank processes by value: volume, handling time, errors, customer impact and regulation
Design processes once and configure them by region, brand and partner
Apply a clear automation order: API first, RPA where there's no API, people where judgment matters
Bring in AI where it pays: document intake, triage, next-best action and handler summaries
Give handlers one workspace for cases, documents and customer context
Lead the BPM analyst team and set standards for process design and requirements
Act as Product Owner with our SI partner: epics, acceptance criteria, sprint reviews and sign-off
Plan rollout, training and adoption with operations leaders in each region

What skills and experience you’ll bring on this journey:

10+ years in product management, operations transformation or BPM
5+ years owning a case management or BPM platform such as Pega, Appian, Camunda or ServiceNow
A track record of automation that measurably cut handling time or cost
Experience rolling out a shared platform across regions or business units
Strong process design skills: BPMN, Lean, SLAs and work allocation
Experience leading analysts and managing SI partners and vendors
The credibility to bring operations and technology leaders to one plan

Nice to have

Insurance claims, policy servicing or assistance operations experience
Migration from legacy claims or case systems
AI in operations: document intake, triage or agent assist
Lean Six Sigma certification
BPM platform or Scrum Product Owner certification

Why you’ll love working with us!

We value optimism, caring, togetherness, reliability, results-orientation, and forward-thinking.

We have more than 3000 employees worldwide. We are a global group of digital specialists, actuaries, marketers, doctors, nurses, case managers, claims specialists, finance experts, customer service and corporate services professionals. We share a global purpose to look after travellers, at every step of their journey.

Job flexibility. We understand the importance of making sure that work fits into your life, not the other way around. Our hybrid approach ensures you can maintain work-life balance with the flexibility of 3 days in the office and 2 days working from home, after an initial training period.

Career growth. This is an extremely exciting time for us at Zurich Cover-More, as we rapidly expand our business across the globe. We’re committed to helping our people thrive through a comprehensive onboarding experience, continuous professional development, and a supportive work environment that empowers growth at every stage of your career.

Take the time you need, for you and your community. We encourage you to take the time you need when you need it. We offer regular annual and personal leave benefits along with anniversary leave, volunteer leave and a comprehensive paid parental leave scheme.

Diversity and inclusion. We respect who you are and thoroughly embrace diversity. Wherever life has taken you, we welcome you to bring your whole self to work. Just be you – because that’s exactly who we’re looking for.

We also offer some other perks including:

Mediclaim insurance cover in case of any health emergency
Coverage under group personal accident insurance
Flexible and compressed work weeks and hybrid working options.
Generous range of paid leave – 21 annual leave days, 6 sick leave days, 12 public holidays
An extra day off for you to take on your birthday or your annual work anniversary.

Appy today and let’s go to great places together!

Addepar unifies portfolio, market and client data in a total portfolio view and delivers AI-powered insights within investment and client workflows. In addition to our core values, Addepar is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

PHISHING SCAM WARNING: Addepar is among several companies recently made aware of a phishing scam involving con artists posing as hiring managers recruiting via email, text and social media. Role: Product Manager, Trading Infrastructure
You will own the professional and algo trading surface of Arrow: the products where latency, data depth and execution quality are the whole point. Five areas sit in your remit, and each one is a product in its own right.

TBT charts: In-house tick-by-tick charting: sub-second candles, order-flow and footprint views, replay, with chart latency held close to feed latency
HFT algos: In-house algos and a strategy marketplace retail traders can deploy on co-located infrastructure, with risk guardrails and exchange approvals built in
API latency: The trading and market-data APIs: round-trip order latency at p50/p95/p99, WebSocket feed delivery, SDK ergonomics, rate limits, sandbox
Colocation access: Productizing exchange co-lo for clients: rack and VM offerings, provisioning, cross-connects, pricing and compliance
Tick-level data: Dissemination of full-depth, tick-by-tick market data: live feeds, snapshots, historical tick archives, entitlements and fan-out at scale

As one of the first Product Managers on the Arrow team, you will work directly with the CTO, quants, the HFT desk, and connectivity engineers. You won't just follow a product process—you will help build it from scratch. In this role, you will spend just as much time analyzing order books and latency data as you do planning roadmaps.

You'll do:
Own the TBT charting roadmap. Define what a tick-by-tick chart must do for a scalper that a one-second chart cannot: sub-second aggregation, order-flow and footprint views, volume-at-price, replay, and multi-instrument sync. Set and track the chart-update latency budget against the raw feed.
Bring in-house HFT algos to retail. Scope the first algos and the strategy marketplace: which strategies ship first, how traders discover, configure and deploy them on co-located infrastructure, what the kill switches and position limits look like, and how each algo clears SEBI and exchange approval before launch.
Own API latency as a product metric. Define the order round-trip and feed-delivery SLOs at p50, p95 and p99, instrument them end to end (client, gateway, OMS, exchange), publish them transparently, and drive the engineering backlog that moves them.
Run the developer experience for the trading API: Go and Python SDKs, WebSocket market-data streams, docs, sandbox, rate limits, static-IP and algo-tagging requirements, and onboarding for API clients from first key to first live order.
Productise colocation access. Turn exchange co-lo into something a professional client can buy: rack, VM and managed-server tiers, provisioning SLAs, cross-connects, pricing, and the compliance and audit trail each exchange requires.
Own tick-level data dissemination. Define the market-data products: full-depth live feeds, TBT versus snapshot tiers, historical tick archives, entitlements and billing, and the fan-out architecture needed to serve thousands of clients without adding latency.
Talk to professional traders every week: scalpers, option market-makers, quants and API users. Turn what they say and what their order flow shows into specs engineers can build from without a second meeting.
Write crisp PRDs with success metrics, latency budgets, failure modes and exchange-rule constraints (algo approval, order-to-trade ratios, throttles, circuit limits, square-off timings) spelled out.
Partner with the CTO, the HFT desk and exchange-connectivity engineers on trade-offs between latency, throughput, reliability and features; a feature that adds 200 µs to the hot path is a product decision, not just an engineering one.
Define and track the metrics that matter: order latency and feed latency by percentile, API uptime, active API clients, algo deployments and their P&L distribution, co-lo utilisation, and tick-data subscriptions.

What we're looking for:
4-8 years in product, trading-systems engineering or quant/HFT trading, with at least 3 years owning a technical or fintech product end to end.
You understand market microstructure. Order books, tick data, matching-engine behaviour, order-to-trade ratios, what co-lo buys you and what it does not. You know why a scalper cares about the difference between 1 ms and 3 ms.

Required: Experience using or building incident-management platforms and solutions, including defining workflows, product requirements, integrations, service-level measures, dashboards, and capabilities supporting incident intake, triage, escalation, resolution, communication, and post-incident improvement.

Title: Product Manager - Logistics & Delivery
Department: Product

About us : 
Since 2017, ClickPost has been the post-purchase intelligence platform that turns logistics complexity into a competitive advantage for the world's leading retailers, including Walmart, Nykaa, Mars, Adidas, Bluestone, GIVA, Kapiva, and 600+ brands across India, Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and North America. Through a single API, our platform manages tracking, exceptions, and returns across 700+ pre-integrated carriers, with AI allocating every shipment to the optimal carrier and resolving delivery issues before orders fail.
And we're not standing still. We're actively building the agentic layer for post-purchase, from AI voice agents like Parth to a growing suite of agents that resolve delivery exceptions, confirm orders, and recover lost sales. This is real, in-production AI, live with customers today.
We process 50M+ shipments every month, helping brands cut failed deliveries and "where-is-my-order" queries while converting more returns into exchanges.
We're one of the rare companies operating at the intersection of cutting-edge AI, enormous scale, and a brand respected across the global SaaS and e-commerce world. Our core values of transparency, continuous learning, ownership, and speed, plus a team that includes several ex-startup founders, make this a place that's both fast-moving and rich with opportunities to learn. Our vision is to become the global standard for post-purchase intelligence, where logistics complexity never limits a brand's growth.

About the Role:
We help e-commerce brands ship millions of orders through many delivery partners. Behind every order are a few simple questions. Which delivery partners can reach this customer? Which one is the best choice for this order? When will it actually arrive? And what happens when something goes wrong?
You'll own the products that answer those questions, along with the AI agents we're building on top of them.

We're looking for an AI-native PM. You'll own AI products, and you'll also use AI for most of your own work. You'll use AI coding tools like Claude Code or Cursor to analyze data, build simulations, prototype agent workflows, investigate issues, and turn your repeated tasks into reusable tools.
Something that takes a traditional PM a week with an analyst and an engineer should take you an afternoon.

What you will do:

1.Delivery coverage
How brands set up which delivery partners can serve which locations.
Making setup faster for new brands and reducing configuration errors and support tickets.
Outcome: Brands go live faster, and fewer orders fail because no suitable delivery partner was available.

2. Delivery partner selection and recommendations
The rules and rankings that decide which delivery partner handles each order.
Balancing cost, speed, delivery success, returns and partner capacity for each brand.
Outcome: Lower cost per delivered order, higher delivery success, and brands that can see why each partner was chosen.

3. Simulation
Running what-if simulations before anything changes in production, like "what happens to cost and delivery time if we move 15% of orders from one partner to another?"
Turning the results into clear recommendations that brands can act on.
Outcome: Every major change is backed by a simulation before it goes live.

4. Delivery date promise
How accurate the delivery date shown to shoppers is, how often we miss it, and how that affects the brand's sales and customer experience.
Outcome: Shoppers see delivery dates they can trust, and brands see fewer complaints about late orders.

5. AI agents
Defining and shipping AI agents that recommend strategies, explain performance changes, and answer customer questions on their own.
Owning the evaluation: when the agent is right, when it's wrong, and how we know which.
Outcome: Agents that resolve a measurable share of questions end to end, with answers people can trust and act on

6. Data analysis and customer issue resolution
Digging into large datasets to answer questions like "why did this partner's share of orders jump last week?" or "why did delivery success drop in this region?"
Owning customer escalations from the moment they're reported until they're closed, and turning the patterns you see into product fixes.
Outcome: Faster answers for customers, and fewer of the same issues coming back.

How you'll work:
You build things yourself. Use AI coding tools to write SQL, Python scripts and simulations, and build working prototypes without waiting for engineering bandwidth.
You automate what you repeat. If you investigate the same type of issue twice, the third time it should be a reusable script, tool or agent workflow.
You turn your knowledge into something AI can use. Write the guides, knowledge bases and prompts that our AI agents and internal teams rely on.
You test AI properly. Define evaluations, test against real cases, find the failure modes, and know when an agent is confidently wrong.
You prototype before you write the spec. Show engineering a working prototype instead of a 10-page document whenever you can.
You own outcomes end-to-end. Write clear PRDs, then stay involved through build, testing, rollout and adoption. Track your products' metrics every week and act when they drift.
You work across teams. Work directly with Engineering, Data Science, Customer Success, Sales and customers.

What success looks like: First 90 Days
First 30 days: You understand how our core products work end-to-end, you've investigated real customer cases, and you've resolved your first few escalations on your own.
By 90 days: You own one or two product areas outright, you've shipped at least one meaningful improvement, and you've delivered at least one simulation-backed recommendation to a customer.
By 6 months: Your products' metrics (delivery date accuracy, recommendation quality, escalation volume, agent accuracy) have measurably improved, and you've automated a meaningful share of your own recurring work.

What we're looking for:

Must have:
3 to 5 years in product management, preferably in B2B SaaS, logistics, e-commerce, fintech or marketplaces.
You use AI daily, in depth. You regularly use AI coding tools and LLMs to build and analyse things, not only to write emails. You can show us what you've built.
Strong with data. SQL and Excel at scale, plus enough Python, with AI assistance, to run your own analysis and simulations.
Comfortable with technical detail. You can read API docs and logs, and discuss trade-offs with engineers.
You understand how LLMs behave. You know about context, tool use, hallucinations, evaluations, and when to use an LLM versus fixed rules.
A record of shipping. Concrete examples of features you took to production, with measurable impact.
High ownership and urgency. You close loops, unblock other teams, escalate early with a proposed fix, and don't need follow-ups.
Structured thinking. You can take a vague customer complaint and break it down into root causes.
Good to have:
Experience in logistics, supply chain or e-commerce operations.
Experience with recommendation, ranking, optimisation or forecasting products.
You've built your own AI agents, tools or automations.
You've shipped an LLM-powered feature to real users and handled what broke afterwards.
A GitHub profile, a portfolio, or side projects that show you build things.
Startup or zero-to-one experience.

What You Can Expect:
Ownership and autonomy: You'll own and drive problems end-to-end, with no micro-management.
Culture: We value speed and expect you to move fast and stay updated with the latest in ML and AI. People grow extremely fast at ClickPost when they focus on impact and take initiative.
Our team thrives on transparency.
Compensation: Competitive salary plus performance bonus.

Generous leave policy
Learning and development budget
